articles.title: Paul Pogba and Paris welcome NFL to France, Cam Skattebo is out of the dog house and Jared Goff is an MVP contender - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo starred for the New York Giants in a shock win over the Houston Texans, while Tee Higgins enjoyed a big day to lead the Cincinnati Bengals past the Baltimore Ravens; watch the NFL return to Madrid as the Bengals face the Atlanta Falcons on November 8, live on Sky Sports NFL
articles.body:
The league pitched up for its historic French bow amid a period of civil unrest across France, with violence and looting having prompted heightened security measures heading into the weekend along with the cancellation of fan activations designed to ramp up the pre-game flavour.

As much contributes to the strong belief that the NFL will return to Paris for another game next year, with the league not only eager to establish a permanent presence in these international markets but perhaps also utilise a calmer and more accurate window in which to fairly flaunt one of the most iconic cities on the planet.

Nevertheless, for all that might have been said about safety concerns, football proceeded as planned on Sunday as the Pittsburgh Steelers beat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 at the Stade de France, which added NFL to a brimming resume already including the World Cup final, Euros final and Rhianna, Rolling Stones and Coldplay concerts, to name just a few.

The gameday presentation itself was spectacular and everything Paris could have envisioned, controlled 'No pyro no party' exhibitions joining Pittsburgh's Terrible Towels and an injection of Mardis Gras-style entertainment in forging the NFL's desired 'mini-Super Bowl' feel in celebration of yet another first for football. It also came with a stunning rendition of the French national anthem, as well as a half-time show courtesy of Burna Boy.

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Pogba was on the field taking photographs pre-game, while France rugby union captain Antoine Dupont and nine-time world champion judoka Teddy Riner were both in attendance, the latter receiving one of the loudest roars of the afternoon.

Cam Jordan and Alvin Kamara leading the WHO DAT Saints chants with a raucous Stade de France crowd on strings was enough to raise the hairs on your arm, while the discovery that 'blitz' translates to 'charge surprise' in French - courtesy of a good friend from another media outlet - was enough to let me once again appreciate the magic of taking football across the world.

It had also been reinforced by the manner in which cries of 'WHO DAT' around tourist hot-spots would light up any given Saints fan's face, confusion and caution while following a map in an unknown land quickly turning into at-home comfort.

Both the Steelers and Saints fanbases travel well, and there was certainly a dominant American presence compared to locals inside the stadium. It would help create a typical US gameday atmosphere, which was perhaps needed given how the week had gone; what might not have helped was the stadium reportedly running out of food at concessions stands during the game.

For what it is worth, Aaron Rodgers might be right to double down on the value in teams arriving on the Monday of a game-week for international matchups. The Steelers quarterback lamented his side's Friday morning landing, underlining his desire to spend more time in the city. As far as introducing football and teams and the NFL's superstars to new markets around the world is concerned, he is right.

Paris features among a record nine international games being played in the 2026 season, becoming one of the NFL's newest host territories alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro while preceding upcoming contests in Madrid, Munich and Mexico City. Commissioner Roger Goodell spoke this week of plans to play in Tokyo in either 2027 or 2028, and it feels increasingly likely the league will return to Dublin after the Steelers beat the Minnesota Vikings in Ireland last season.

The French will get another chance to showcase the beautiful best of Paris. The build-up may have been dampened, the rain may have soggied the mood and the game itself may not have produced fireworks, but there was no hiding from another special moment for the NFL.

The NFC South is WIDE open! Reigning division champions the Carolina Panthers had looked like the team to catch, as the only one over .500 coming into Sunday, where they had the opportunity to stretch further clear from the field with a home victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and with the Atlanta Falcons facing a tough assignment in welcoming the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers to town. The Saints at least held up their end of the bargain by dropping to 2-5 on the year with defeat to the Steelers in Paris, but the Falcons (3-4) inflicted the 49ers' first defeat of the season, while the Panthers (3-3) were handed a 43-13 hammering by the Bucs (2-5) at home - despite the returning Baker Mayfield posting only 64 passing yards! A year on from a three-way tiebreaker being necessary to separate Carolina from Atlanta and Tampa Bay on 8-9 records, does anyone actually want to take over this division?!

Congrats to those of you fortunate enough to have picked up New York Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr in fantasy football this week. Not that I'm bitter or anything! The 30th overall pick in this year's draft out of Indiana - the fifth wideout taken - proved that his 103-yard and one TD outing against the New England Patriots last week was no fluke as he backed it up with a 115-yarder, plus a score, in Sunday's clash with the Miami Dolphins. Both games ended in defeat for the Jets - Miami winning their first of the season - to suggest that this isn't quite yet the brave new era in New York that Jets fans dream of, but Cooper is at least placing himself at the heart of things for if and when it does finally arrive. To help accelerate that process, the 2-5 Jets may well be sellers before the November 10 trade deadline, to build themselves greater draft capital for the future. As such, the emergence of Cooper could signal the end of Garrett Wilson's tenure in NYC. He had only two receptions for 26 yards against the Dolphins, and there'd be no shortage of takers for his talent.

An Indianapolis fire-sale feels imminent, and the same failure to find a long-term solution at quarterback that recently saw general manager Chris Ballard fired is also going to cost Shane Steichen his job. Daniel Jones struggled once more as the Colts suffered a 16-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, who blitzed the former Giants quarterback on 85.2 per cent of his drop backs - the highest blitz rate by any defense since the Next Gen Stats era began in 2016. A third straight loss leaves the Colts 2-5 and the most likely candidates for an exodus as the trade deadline approaches on November 10. Star running back Jonathan Taylor, guard Quenton Nelson and veteran defensive lineman DeForest Buckner have all been linked to trades as another rebuild lurks.

The Las Vegas Raiders-Kirk Cousins vibes are over. It happens to the best of us in Sin City. You're with your friends on a hot streak at the blackjack table, the rest of the casino floor peering over like meerkats to investigate the clamour coming from your cohort as every card hits, contrary to expectations. But the fun has to end somewhere.

Sure, that isn't to say the Raiders and Cousins have played their hand, because there is no shame in losing to a Los Angeles Rams team battling to turn their season around, but four straight defeats for Klint Kubiak's side has undone their early momentum. It should also be noted those four losses have come to legitimate contenders in the New England Patriots, Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills and now the Rams. Cousins also threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns at the weekend, so it isn't quite panic stations that might prompt a premature turn to Fernando Mendoza. But just a reminder of overreacting to early weeks of the season, when the Raiders were surprising us all.

Cam Skattebo: In fact, the whole Giants backfield can count themselves as winners, really, as Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr joined Skattebo in finding the end zone in the overtime win over the Houston Texans. Heck, even benched QB Jameis Winston got in.

But Skattebo is no doubt the headline-grabber, a week on from having zero touches in the Giants' defeat to the New Orleans Saints after fumble troubles in their prior tie with the Washington Commanders. Seventeen carries, for 124 yards and a score in New York's downing of the much-hyped Texans defense means Skattebo is surely now out of coach John Harbaugh's dog house.

Jared Goff: I'm not sure football gives Jared Goff his flowers enough. The Lions quarterback should be in the MVP discussion right now, bolstering his case on Sunday as he went 22 of 32 for 303 yards and two touchdown passes to lead Detroit past the Packers, in doing so becoming the first quarterback in history to post at least 14 touchdown passes and no turnovers through his first six games of a season. He has now thrown for 1,788 yards and his 14 scores so far this season, completing 150 of his 223 pass attempts while having been yet to surrender an interception.

Houston Texans defense: The 2025 Texans defense ranked as the NFL's best in yards allowed - just 277.2 per game - and were second only to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in scoring, with a mere 17.4 conceded per game. They also had 29 takeaways on the year to rank third in the league.

This season, with much still expected of largely the same unit, they can be described as middling - at best - as they quite literally rank middle of the road for YPG allowed (329.0 15 th ) and PPG coughed up (23.8, 20 th ). A fifth defeat in seven to start the season, with their overtime loss against the New York Giants, now has them in big trouble to make the playoffs.

The Ravens: Jesse Minter's Ravens were dealt another blow in a tight AFC North race as their 35-13 defeat to the Bengals left them 4-3 at the bottom of the division. With Lamar Jackson out again, you might have expected a big day for Derrick Henry; instead the Ravens running back finished with just 17 carries for 45 yards after managing only four carries for 13 yards in the second half. His drop off in usage can be a bizarre theme at times, so too Baltimore's continued stutters despite the talent on their roster.

Player of the Weekend - Tee Higgins, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

Tee Higgins had zero catches in the first half of Cincinnati's 35-13 win over the Ravens, bottled up alongside receiving partner in crime Ja'Marr Chase. In the second half alone he made six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown to break Baltimore's resistance with yet another clinic in devastating route-running. At times he can be overlooked in favour of Chase, but make no mistake of his value to Joe Burrow and Cincinnati's Super Bowl chances. He now leads the team with 27 catches for 423 yards and a score.

Here is a nod to J.J. McCarthy and a standout performance in his first start at quarterback for the Giants, who he guided to a surprise 27-21 overtime win against the Texans after taking the reins from Jameis Winston during the week. McCarthy finished 20 of 28 for 252 yards including a stunning deep-shot to Malik Nabers with pressure in his face to reward Harbaugh's faith in the former Vikings play-caller. The win lifts the Giants to 4-2-1 at the top of the NFC East as they continued their playoff quest. McCarthy's big day came a week after he impressed enough with a fourth-quarter cameo against the Saints to dislodge Winston; having arrived via a trade from Minnesota in light of Jaxson Dart's injury, he now has a career to resurrect his NFL career - perhaps even start it.

articles.title: From middle school crush to Super Bowl sideline: How Drake Maye and Ann Michael Hudson built a decade-long romance before the NFL ever knew his name
articles.summary: Drake Maye was 12 when he started dating Ann Michael Hudson.
articles.body: Drake Maye was 12 when he started dating Ann Michael Hudson. He was 23 when he kissed her on the field at Levi's Stadium before Super Bowl LX on February 8, 2026. Between those moments sit ten years of Friday night games, a high school transfer, four years at North Carolina, a beach proposal and a June 2025 wedding. The Patriots lost to Seattle 29-13, yet the couple had already become one of New England's favorite stories of the season. Here is how it all came together.How Drake Maye and Ann Michael Hudson's romance began in middle schoolThe two started dating as seventh graders in North Carolina in 2015. Ann Michael has embraced that origin story herself. In a 2024 TikTok, she captioned a video of the pair "So middle school."They both attended William A. Hough High School in Cornelius, where Maye played quarterback for the Hough Huskies. Hudson was in the stands on Friday nights. Maye later transferred to Myers Park High School to play football, and the relationship held. When he moved on to North Carolina, her Friday nights simply became Saturday afternoons.Football ran through her family, too. Her younger brother, Tad Hudson, also played quarterback at North Carolina and overlapped with Maye there. So she was never just a girlfriend watching from a distance. She grew up around the position.Maye made things public on Instagram on New Year's Day 2020. His caption read "Bringing in ’20 with a 10." By then, the relationship was already more than four years old. Most fans only met Ann Michael after the story was well underway, which may explain why it felt so settled once they did.How the NFL pulled the couple in different directionsThe Patriots took Maye third overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. At a draft event at Gillette Stadium on April 26, 2024, he introduced his brothers Beau, Cole and Luke, along with his girlfriend since seventh grade, Ann Michael. She posted her own reaction online: "I can't wait for this next chapter!"That chapter started with distance. Maye moved to New England for his rookie season, and Ann Michael stayed in Chapel Hill to finish college. She graduated in 2025. It was a demanding stretch for a young quarterback who was learning a new city and a new playbook while the person who knew him best was hundreds of miles away. He also became the Patriots' starter in the middle of that season, so the pressure only grew.Then the season ended, and Maye proposed on a beach in January 2025. They married in North Carolina on June 21, 2025. That was five months after the engagement and almost exactly a decade after they first started dating. Few NFL quarterbacks can say their marriage is older in spirit than their pro career.Why Ann Michael Maye became a Patriots fan favoriteNobody planned this part. During the 2025 season, Ann Michael went viral on TikTok for her "Bakemas" videos, where she shared recipes for sweet treats. Patriots fans filled her comment section with love, and some started calling her the "First Lady of New England."The appeal makes sense when you think about it. Her content had nothing to do with football strategy or celebrity. It was cookies and cakes from a woman who had been around the team's quarterback since middle school. Fans got a way into the Patriots that did not involve a depth chart.It spread into the locker room, too. Several Patriots players were asked about her treats during Super Bowl week, and Maye was asked to rank them. He seemed happy to play along. He called watching New England embrace his wife the "coolest" part of the season. "It's been awesome to follow her journey," he said.That detail matters. Plenty of athletes talk about supporting a partner's career. Maye sounded like someone who simply enjoyed watching it happen.What the Super Bowl loss showed about the coupleThe football season itself was remarkable. The Patriots went 14-3, won the AFC East and reached Super Bowl LX one year after finishing 4-13. Maye finished second in MVP voting, behind Matthew Stafford, in only his second season.The final game was rough. Seattle sacked him six times, and he committed three turnovers. The Patriots were shut out for the first three quarters. Maye also said his throwing shoulder had been injected with painkillers and he could not feel it much. Late in the game, he set a Super Bowl record with 235 passing yards in a quarter, but by then the result was settled.Ann Michael's response came a few days later on Instagram. She wrote, "Not how we wanted it to end but still thanking God for this incredible season." Maye's own outlook was just as steady. "I have a beautiful wife. I look forward to spending this offseason with my wife," he said.A loss on that stage can swallow a young quarterback whole. It helps to have someone who met him long before the stats, the contract or the cameras. A few days before kickoff, Maye had said he would advise all of his teammates to get married at some point. After the game, you could see why he meant it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Jared Goff earns $55 million in 2026 under his $212 million contract as his estimated net worth reaches $100 million
articles.summary: Jared Goff will collect $55 million in cash from the Detroit Lions in 2026, the biggest yearly payout of his four-year, $212 million extension.
articles.body: Jared Goff will collect $55 million in cash from the Detroit Lions in 2026, the biggest yearly payout of his four-year, $212 million extension. The deal averages $53 million a year and holds about $170.6 million in guarantees, according to Spotrac. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his wealth at $100 million. Both figures need context. Detroit reworked his contract in March to free up $32 million in cap room, and his paychecks have arrived in lumpy amounts since 2024. Goff turned 32 this month, and his biggest guaranteed paydays are arriving now.How Jared Goff earns $55 million in 2026 under his $212 million dealThe $55 million is plain base salary. Spotrac's year-by-year breakdown shows no signing bonus, roster bonus or incentive money stacked on top. NFL teams pay base salary in 18 weekly installments during the regular season, so Jared Goff's gross check works out to roughly $3 million a week. That is before taxes and fees.The best part for Goff is the protection. His 2026 salary is fully guaranteed. Twenty million dollars was locked in when he signed in May 2024, and the other $35 million became guaranteed early in the 2025 league year. A bad season or a serious injury cannot take that money away.The wider package also shows how badly Detroit wanted him. The extension includes a full no-trade clause, so the Lions cannot move him without his consent. On the day the deal was announced, Goff talked about winning, not money. He said he was more driven and more fired up than ever to push harder and bring a Super Bowl to the city.The Lions have had reason to trust that. Goff threw for 4,564 yards and 34 touchdowns in 2025 with only eight interceptions, his lowest total since 2022. He did that with a new offensive coordinator. This year brought another new play-caller in Drew Petzing.Why his 2025 pay was $18 million and 2026 is three times biggerJared Goff's cash schedule looks strange until you remember the signing bonus. Detroit paid $73 million up front in 2024, which pushed his cash that year to $80.6 million. After that, the checks settled into a different rhythm. Spotrac lists $18 million for 2025, $55 million for 2026, $40 million for 2027 and $47 million for 2028.That is why the $212 million headline and the $53 million average can mislead. Nobody earns $53 million in a typical year. Goff got far more than that in 2024, far less in 2025, and a little more in 2026. NFL deals are built around cap room and guarantees, not even installments.The later years carry less certainty. About $22 million of his 2027 salary was injury-guaranteed at signing. It breaks into two parts: $18 million became fully guaranteed in March 2026, and another $4 million locks in this coming March. The 2028 season is where the Lions hold an exit. Spotrac marks it as a potential out with $14.6 million in dead cap, and it includes a $7 million roster bonus due in March 2028.So the practical commitment sits closer to $193.6 million through 2027, the figure Spotrac treats as the real value of the deal. Whether Goff plays out 2028 at age 34 will depend on how he looks over the next season and a half.What Jared Goff's March 2026 contract restructure really changedGoff agreed to the restructure on March 11, and Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reported it. The Lions needed the space. One offseason projection had them nearly $17 million over the 2026 cap before they could sign any free agents. The room helped Detroit rebuild an offensive line that lost left tackle Taylor Decker and center Graham Glasgow.Restructures like this usually turn part of a player's base salary into a bonus and spread it over the remaining years. The team saves room today and carries bigger cap charges later. The player's cash stays the same. Spotrac's public page still shows $55 million for 2026, though the updated cap table sits behind its paywall, so the exact new cap hit is unconfirmed.The trade-off is real. Before the rework, Spotrac listed his 2026 cap hit at $69.6 million, about 23.8 percent of the league cap. Pushing money into future seasons likely makes 2027 and 2028 costlier to walk away from, and it can shrink the value of that 2028 exit. Detroit gets freedom in free agency now and a heavier bill down the road.How Jared Goff's $100 million net worth adds upStart with earnings. Spotrac counts $161 million through 2023 and $80.6 million in 2024. Add 2025 and 2026, and his career cash reaches about $315 million by the end of this season. Celebrity Net Worth uses a smaller tally of $187.7 million through 2024, so the trackers clearly count bonuses differently.Why does net worth sit so far below earnings? Taxes take the biggest bite. Federal income tax tops out at 37 percent, and state taxes depend on where he lives and where he plays. Agents take a slice, and life at this level is expensive. Athletes keep far less than the headline number. That is a general rule, not a disclosed figure for Goff.Outside income helps but stays small next to salary. Celebrity Net Worth puts his endorsements near $2 million a year, with past partners including Red Bull, BMW, Bose, Banana Republic, Nike and Pizza Hut. He also launched a clothing line, JG16, in 2019. Real estate adds a quieter layer. He paid $10.5 million for a Manhattan Beach home in 2023. He sold a Hidden Hills house for $6.4 million in 2022 after buying it for $4 million in 2018.One caution on the $100 million figure. The profile was last updated in May 2024, the same month he signed the extension. Two more years of large checks have landed since, so the estimate may trail reality. It is still an estimate, not an audited number.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ $1.625 million commitment to youth programs reveals another side of his legacy beyond Super Bowl wins and major deals
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, his wife Brittany and the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation have put $1.625 million behind the Boys & Girls Clubs of America.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, his wife Brittany and the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation have put $1.625 million behind the Boys & Girls Clubs of America. The foundation announced the multi-year commitment as a new national partnership on October 4, 2023. It will also give $1,500 for every touchdown the Chiefs quarterback produces in the regular season. The news came right after Mahomes agreed to a restructured deal with Kansas City, which gave the timing a little extra weight.Mahomes foundation commits $1.625 million to Boys & Girls ClubsThe core of the deal is simple. The foundation is making a $1.625 million contribution and a multi-year commitment. The money is meant for the clubs nationwide, but the couple pointed first to the places that shaped them. Those are Greater Kansas City and Lubbock, Texas. Local reports also named Tyler and Whitehouse, the East Texas towns tied to Patrick's childhood and to where he met Brittany.The touchdown pledge adds a second layer, and it moves with his play. Mahomes had eight touchdowns when the news broke ahead of Week 5. By that math, the pledge already stood at $12,000 and was still climbing. It also gives every Chiefs fan a small stake in the box score.Brittany's story is part of this. She attended a club herself as a child, and Patrick said kids in those programs get the tools to "lead with compassion and purpose." That personal link is what separates this from a donation signed off by an accountant.Where the money goes in Kansas City, Lubbock and East TexasThe plan is specific. The clubs in Kansas City and Lubbock will each rename one facility after the foundation, and the foundation will help upgrade both. The East Texas club will offer scholarships for up to 300 young people a year at no cost.Scholarships repeat every year. A building gets repaired once, but 300 free memberships have to be funded again each season. That is why the multi-year wording matters more than the headline number.The foundation was not starting from scratch. It already runs Read for 15, Volunteer for 15 and 15 for 15. One reading rally drew nearly 2,400 elementary students from 16 local schools. In 2022, 539 young volunteers logged 12,844 service hours, and the 2023 goal was more than 800 youth and 15,000 hours. Mahomes was also the Chiefs' finalist for the Walter Payton Man of the Year award for the 2022 season, largely because of this youth work.Brittany summed up the thinking in one line: "We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others." The clubs now have a funding source that does not depend on a single check, and Kansas City and Lubbock will soon have buildings that carry the foundation's name.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers, in vintage form, takes shots at Saints on the field and the NFL off it
articles.summary: In contrast — of course — to the usual narrative that the NFL has too many international games, Rodgers endorsed the overseas slate, and wished the NFL would...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers still has his moments. They're moments now, not drives and certainly not games, but they're enough to stay in yet another playoff hunt for one more year.

Every once in a while, Rodgers gives us reason to remember that he's more than just the (pick your side) surly/clever, smug/knowledgeable conspiracy theorist/truth teller that he's positioned himself as over the past few years. It doesn't happen much anymore, but every once in a while, Rodgers rears back, slings a moon-scraper of a pass, and reminds us that, yes, he's a first-ballot Hall of Famer no matter how infuriating he is behind a mic.

That throwback throw came in the course of Pittsburgh's win over New Orleans on Sunday in France , a game mostly notable for being as unappetizing as a nine-day-old baguette. How bad was Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory? Put it this way: until he knelt down twice to end the game, Rodgers had more yards rushing than any Saint — and at that point, Rodgers had all of 8 yards rushing.

Rodgers effectively iced the game with a scramble — yes, really — late in the fourth quarter when the black-and-gold sea parted and he decided to go yolo into a wide-open French meadow:

The Steelers exulted on the sideline, congratulating Rodgers as if he'd just thrown another touchdown pass. He didn't miss the "backhanded compliment," as he put it, but he enjoyed it nonetheless.

"I'm a lot more reticent to run these days. I'm just not very fast anymore," Rodgers smiled after the game. "Sometimes you gotta suck it up and make a play for your guys, and I think because I am so much less athletic than I used to be, it actually fires up [the team]."

Rodgers set a more notable mark in the course of the game. That pass to DK Metcalf set up a touchdown pass to Darnell Washington that marked Rodgers' 540th career passing touchdown, one more than Peyton Manning. Only Drew Brees and Tom Brady are ahead of Rodgers, but it's unlikely he'll catch them; Brees is 31 touchdowns ahead.

Still, hitting that mark — and delivering that beauty of a 51-yarder — is a reminder of just how much Aaron Rodgers has done in this league. Rodgers is in his sunset days in the NFL, with 10 regular-season games left and, perhaps, one last playoff run. Rodgers' off-field matters — the bombs he drops during "Pat McAfee" appearances, the will-he-or-won't-he retirement guessing games, the perpetual squabbles with his coaches — overshadow his on-field performance. But those moments Sunday were a reminder that maybe, just maybe, he's got a couple more gems left to reveal.

And speaking of off-field Rodgers, after the game, he busted out more vintage material, going all just-asking-questions on the NFL's international game strategy. In contrast — of course — to the usual narrative that the NFL has too many international games, Rodgers endorsed the international slate, and wished the NFL would have gone further to push American football into international markets.

Rodgers said he'd approved of the idea to send more NFL teams to international destinations as far back as the early 2010s. Instead, "the owners wanted to push for 17 games for the extra revenue, and because they care so much about player safety," he deadpanned.

"I wish there was a mandate from the league — they would have to open up their pocketbooks, maybe [they're] a little tight on money and stuff — but I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. You can do events in those cities and outreach stuff and community work," he said, "but they won't, because they're a little tight."

That's the kind of thing you say when you have no fear whatsoever of retribution from the commissioner's office because you know you'll be out the door and out from under the NFL umbrella no later than Valentine's Day.

Back to the football field. Rodgers and Pittsburgh have the chance to take over sole possession of first place in the division in just one week when Cleveland comes to town. The rest of the season offers up the standard run through the division, plus games against Philadelphia, Carolina, Houston and Tennessee. Tough matches against Jacksonville and Denver loom, but that's a November-December problem.

For now, Rodgers and the Steelers are plodding their way toward one more postseason. They're not speedy, they're not pretty, but they're still moving forward. And for Rodgers, in his one last ride, that's more than enough.

articles.title: Sports equinox 2026: Date, schedule, meaning and history behind the rare event
articles.summary: The 33rd sports equinox will occur in 2026.
articles.body:
Sports fans are in for an extra special treat just days before Halloween in 2026. The sports equinox is Monday, offering fans a bevy of exciting games to watch on what — in a just world — should be one of the biggest holidays of the year.

The slate should be exciting in 2026, as a number of prominent teams will take their respective fields, courts or rinks this year. With so much action, sports fans face one big question: Which games should they prioritize on such an action-packed sports day?

Below, is everything sports fans need to know about the 2026 sports equinox.

A sports equinox occurs when MLB, NBA, NFL and NHL hold games on the same day. A sports equinox isn't limited to just those leagues, but those four leagues are necessary for the day to be considered a sports equinox.

Due to MLB's schedule, the sports equinox typically occurs in the fall, usually in October. Since the NBA, NFL and NHL are always in season during the month, the sports equinox is often dependent on the World Series, which has consistently been pushed into late October or early November in recent years.

In 2026, the sports equinox will take place Monday.

Here is a list of every single MLB, NBA, NFL and NHL game being played on Monday:

Both organizations will continue the fight for their first-ever World Series title. The Brewers won the first two games in Milwaukee as the series now moves to Tampa Bay. Freddy Peralta is expected to start for the Rays against the Brewers' Robert Gasser.

The Timberwolves looked incredibly strong on opening night, scoring a Western Conference-best 131 points in in a win over the Miami Heat. The Cavaliers, who blew a 29-point lead to the Philadelphia 76ers in their opener, are looking to take the Eastern Conference crown back from the Pistons. • Chicago Bulls vs. Boston Celtics (7:30 p.m. ET) • Dallas Mavericks vs. Miami Heat (7:30 p.m. ET)

Giannis Antetokounmpo showed out on opening night, dropping 35 points in his game in Miami but the Heat so far remain winless. Mavericks second-year star Cooper Flagg put up 32 points in a loss to the Houston Rockets in the opener, but missed Dallas' last game with a shoulder injury. • Indiana Pacers vs. Milwaukee Bucks (8 p.m. ET) • Phoenix Suns vs. Oklahoma City Thunder (8 p.m. ET)

The Thunder and Suns had some bad blood after last year's playoff matchup. While Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander insisted Dillon Brooks' antics weren't an issue in the series, the Thunder star still took a shot at Brooks once the Thunder advanced. That rivalry should continue Monday. • Atlanta Hawks vs. Houston Rockets (8:30 p.m. ET) • Memphis Grizzlies vs. Utah Jazz (9 p.m. ET) • Golden State Warriors vs. Denver Nuggets (10 p.m. ET)

Stephen Curry vs. Nikola Jokic … what more needs to be said? It should be a close contest, as both teams split the regular-season series 2-2 last year.

Tanner McKee makes his second start of the season — and first since Jalen Hurts was sidelined due to blood clots. While the Cowboys don't present the scariest matchup, a win by Philadelphia would go a long way toward the team getting back into the NFC East race after losing four straight games. Dallas, similarly, is in desperate need of a win after dropping its past two contests.

Connor McDavid is out to a record-breaking start this season. He'll look to continue his quest for a 200-point season Monday night against the Red Wings.

While the WNBA is not technically included as part of the sports equinox, the league is playing a pretty important game Monday, Oct. 26.

The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries will square off in Game 5 of the WNBA Finals at 8 p.m. ET. The Valkyries won Game 4 to even the series at two games apiece.

While MLS and NWSL games can sometimes occur on the sports equinox, that won't be the case in 2026, as neither league will hold games Monday.

The sports equinox has taken place 32 other times prior to 2026. This year will mark the 33rd time a sports equinox has occurred.

Here's a full list of each date of a sports equino x, per Sports Reference:

As that list shows, the sports equinox takes place in October the majority of the time. Twenty-four of the 33 sports equinoxes took place during the month. Six have occurred in November and three have taken place in September.

While a sports equinox was more common in the '70s, there was a large gap where it was an extremely rare event. But as MLB has pushed back the World Series, the sports equinox has become more likely since 2015.

There are also some years in which the sports equinox occurred multiple times. That won't be the case in 2026, as the World Series won't line up on another day in which the NFL is playing.

An equinox is a real thing that has nothing to do with sports. The event occurs when the sun appears in line with the Earth's equator. Because of that, both the Northern and Southern Hemisphere of the planet receives roughly equal amounts of daytime and nighttime , per National Geographic. An actual equinox occurs twice a year, once in March and once in September.

articles.title: “It's a family": Travis Kelce makes emotional admission about Patrick Mahomes as Chiefs chase another Super Bowl title

articles.body: Winning three Super Bowl titles together has given Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes plenty to celebrate, but their bond goes beyond touchdowns and championship rings. As the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for their Week 7 clash with the Seattle Seahawks, Kelce has offered insight into what makes the team so difficult to beat. For the veteran tight end, success starts with trust, respect and a shared sense of belonging. His comments also highlight why the partnership between him and Mahomes remains central to Kansas City's ambitions as the team looks to extend its perfect start to the 2026 season.Travis Kelce explains how the Chiefs' family culture drives successThe Chiefs entered Week 7 with an unbeaten 5-0 record, and Kelce believes the atmosphere inside the organisation plays a major role in that success. Speaking with Mahomes during an interview with Chris Berman, the 37-year-old tight end described a culture that encourages players to support one another and compete for a common goal.“It's a family from the top down,” Kelce said.He explained how that connection can make a difference when the pressure rises during a game.“And the culture, that chemistry you build because it's a family environment — you love the guy even more, you're going to do everything you can to get the job done because of how much you respect that dude and that guy for doing the exact same thing. And on top of that, you gotta have fun while doing it.”For Kelce, the Chiefs' winning environment is built on more than individual talent. Players who trust their teammates are more willing to make sacrifices, stay committed and work through difficult moments together.That philosophy has helped Kansas City remain a major force in the NFL. Kelce and Mahomes have connected for 773 receptions, 9,222 receiving yards and 63 touchdowns across 128 regular-season and postseason games.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce reveal the secret behind their connectionThe relationship between Kelce and Mahomes offers a clear example of the communication that drives the Chiefs' offence. Their understanding developed through countless conversations, practice sessions and shared experiences on the field.Kelce credited his quarterback with helping him reach another level as a player.“My game sure as hell skyrocketed and went up when he got here because his football intelligence and his ability to see the game is like none other.”Mahomes has also explained how their partnership began to take shape in 2018, when he became Kansas City's starting quarterback. After each series during training camp, Kelce would ask what Mahomes had noticed and why he had chosen particular throws.“It started in training camp that first year I was starting, after every series he would ask me what I was seeing, why I wanted to throw it here,” Mahomes said. “Through those conversations, I started understanding what he was seeing. Now he's able to do a lot of freelancing in the offense because we are on the same page.”That early investment in communication continues to pay dividends. articles.title: Micah Parsons called out 2 suspect roughing-the-passer calls that cost the Packers
articles.summary: Micah Parsons couldn't believe his eyes as the Packers got screwed by terrible roughing calls in Detroit.
articles.body:
It's hard enough trying to play defense in the modern NFL. Now try to do it when the offensive players, especially the quarterbacks, usually get all of the benefit of the doubt. That's kind of what happened to the Green Bay Packers against the Detroit Lions on Sunday .

While the Packers made their fair share of self-inflicted mistakes in a close 20-17 defeat, a slew of controversial penalties — especially two roughing-the-passer calls on Detroit quarterback Jared Goff — opened the door to the Lions getting a big NFC North win while sending the Packers to last place in the NFC North. And beyond the frustrated defenders on the field, Packers franchise pass-rushing talisman Micah Parsons, who is still recovering from his ACL tear last season, might have been the biggest critic of said roughing calls.

In reaction, Parsons took to his X account in the middle of the game to tag both the NFL and NFL officiating accounts before furiously telling them that the NFL should switch to flag football if every hit on a quarterback will be roughing. This was Parsons going to bat for his guys for getting screwed in a big divisional game:

Once upon a time, we didn't know what a catch was in the NFL. (We kind of still don't?) Then, we didn't know what interference or illegal contact really was. (We kind of still don't?) Now, after watching the Packers' loss to Detroit, I'm not entirely sure anyone knows what roughing the passer is on a consistent basis.

articles.title: Xavier McKinney Questions Refs After Packers' Loss to Lions, 'A Lot of S--t That Doesn't Make Sense'
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers had a number of costly penalties in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions, and they clearly disagreed with some of the calls made by the officials.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers had a number of costly penalties in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions, and they clearly disagreed with some of the calls made by the officials.

Several members of the team addressed the officiating afterwards, including safety Xavier McKinney, who said that "we all see what's going on." He added that "there's a lot of s--t" that doesn't make sense right now.

The Packers had eight penalties that cost them 81 yards, while the Lions had five penalties for 50 yards. While the difference in penalties wasn't exorbitant, Green Bay perhaps had more costly penalties.

In the third quarter, Devonte Wyatt was called for unnecessary roughness after he tackled Amon-Ra St. Brown a touch too late. The result of the flag was a first down for Detroit, and it gave the Lions the ball on the 11-yard line. They scored two plays later.

"We ruled that the play was over," referee Alex Moore said in an interview with pool reporter Ben Raven of MLive. "I can't honestly hear if there was a whistle over it or not, but the tackler made the tackle, the play was over. Then, there was an additional action, and he basically tackled him again with force after the play was over."

But at the end of the day, the Packers can't blame the loss entirely on the refs. They had a number of preventable errors, like an interception from Jordan Love, a missed field goal late in the game and more.

"I don't even wanna comment on any of the officials," head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters . "It is what it is. You gotta play above it. I thought there were some tough calls, but it is what it is."

Green Bay can't dwell on the loss for too long, as it will have a short week with the Carolina Panthers on deck for Thursday night.

articles.title: NFL fans put on brave face in Paris as Steelers beat Saints with chaos in the city
articles.summary: While NFL fans braved Paris amid civil unrest and violent protests to attend the first-ever game in France, some told OutKick it hasn't been as bad as expected.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints in the NFL’s first-ever game in France that went off surprisingly well despite the protests and civil unrest all week in Paris leading up to the matchup. The NFL was questioned throughout the week after seeing violence, looting, vandalization and more occurring in Paris over widespread anger regarding public living costs, deteriorating public services and more. Even President Donald Trump admitted he was "worried about it," talking about the Steelers-Saints matchup. But the league, despite beloved soccer team Paris Saint-Germaine postponing its Saturday match to Monday due to the unrest, didn’t blink. OutKick caught up with several fans who braved the potential of being caught in the middle of the protests in Paris, and though there were some inconveniences, it didn’t go any further than that for these football goers. "If I’m being honest, I have not seen enough. I’ve seen some graffiti everywhere, but I haven’t seen anything myself," one fan said outside Stade de France. NFL OVERCOMES CIVIL UNREST, TRUMP CONCERNS AND CALLS TO POSTPONE AS STEELERS AND SAINTS KICK OFF IN PARIS Another added: "For the most part, it hasn’t been a problem. It’s not as bad as I was expecting. "There’s a lot of really beautiful things that they’re hurting for no reason. I understand they want to speak their voice, but they’re doing things that shouldn’t be done – vandalizing monuments and stuff. It’s not worth it." Another fan believed that protesters have been going too far when it involves the destruction of property and more violent acts. "Have they gone too far, the protestors? articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 7: Dan Campbell gets bailed out after bonkers fourth-down gamble, and red-zone woes hurt Saints, Ravens and Packers
articles.summary: Red-zone failures were the story in Week 7.
articles.body:
One theme that connected some of the more momentous plays from Sunday's action was where they occurred on the field. The closer you are to the end zone, the more damaging the mistakes tend to be.

We had a major red-zone failure by the Saints in the early game in Paris . Multiple red-zone mistakes followed in the 1 p.m. ET window. And more in the late afternoon slate.

There were also some non-red-zone errors of note, including one that helped prevent another upset in a topsy-turvy Week 7 in the NFL.

Here are some of the more momentous plays from Sunday:

1. Au revoir, points: Tyler Shough's pick sinks Saints in Paris

The Steelers led the Saints, 13-10, at halftime in Paris. New Orleans had the ball first in the second half and was threatening to take the lead in a low-scoring, defensive battle.

After a slow start, it appeared the Saints were gaining steam. QB Tyler Shough converted multiple third downs on a drive that lasted seven-plus minutes and had the Saints cooking with a second-and-7 play at the Steelers' 10-yard line.

That's when linebacker Payton Wilson undercut Chris Olave's route and stepped in front of Shough's pass for a critical interception.

Wilson even tacked on 18 yards on the INT return. The Steelers put up another field goal for a 16-10 lead. Just as important, the Steelers drained off another seven-plus minutes on that drive.

That was the entire third quarter: those two possessions.

The Saints ended up having the ball only six times all game. Turning the ball over on one of those drives, with a great chance to score, ended up proving costly.

2. Passing up field goal hurt Ravens in second-half avalanche

The Ravens led 13-0 at halftime, and there's an argument that they didn't do enough in the first half to pad that lead. Baltimore dominated the first half, possessing the ball for 22-plus minutes, but couldn't build a big enough advantage.

Prior to their first field goal, the Ravens were going for it on fourth-and-1 but they false started, leading to the kick. On the second try, 50 seconds before the half, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter opted not to go for it on fourth-and-3 from the Bengals' 6-yard line.

With Lamar Jackson playing, that's probably a go. With Tyler Huntley starting, Minter went for three points.

The bigger swing might have happened in the second half, when Minter got way more aggressive. The Ravens held the Bengals down badly in the first half defensively, but Joe Burrow unleashed the dragon in the third quarter. After two straight long TD drives, the Bengals were suddenly up, 14-13. The Ravens answered, with Huntley and Derrick Henry moving the ball to the Bengals' 12-yard line. Minter faced a fourth-and-2 decision: kick for the lead or go for it. Minter went for it, and the gamble didn't pay off.

Now, there are a few schools of thought here. Some might argue the Bengals were going to score regardless of whether the Ravens made the field goal. Given the way they moved the ball in the second half, it's fair.

But the Ravens needed to come away with points there and might have also gained a slight psychological edge with the lead. Perhaps they wouldn't have played with the level of desperation they seemed to after halftime.

3. Wonnum's block saved Campbell's bacon

For a 20-17 game, Packers-Lions had a lot going on . Especially in the final five minutes.

The Lions got the ball back after the Packers tied it, 17-17, with just over seven minutes left. They acted like a team that was going to end the game right then and there. After a 9-yard gain on first down, the Lions had back-to-back no-gains.

That set up a fourth-and-1 from his own 24-yard line with just under five minutes remaining. And, boy, that's Dan Campbell's music.

Detroit's head coach went for it, and Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for a 2-yard loss. The Packers were in terrific shape at the Lions' 22-yard line, and had they converted a first down, they'd have put Campbell in a bind with timeouts and the clock.

But it was all moot when the Packers missed on third down and Trey Smack's field-goal try was barely deflected by the Lions' D.J. Wonnum. It's hard to say whether it affected the flight of the ball, but one way or another, the kick missed.

The Lions took the ball down and drained the clock well, with Gibbs smartly refusing to score when the Packers tried to lure him into doing so. It was a win, but a fortunate one, given how Campbell's decision panned out.

"We need to be better as a staff there," Campbell said in his postgame locker-room speech. But he praised Wonnum and his team for toughness in the face of adversity. Self-created adversity at that. Thankfully, Wonnum's block made that decision null and void.

4. Back-to-back turnovers stunted Titans' upset hopes

The Titans stormed out to a 14-0 lead and put the Browns on upset alert early. The Browns chipped away at the deficit with a key second-quarter sequence.

The Browns had regained some momentum with a goal-line stand and a touchdown off a Cam Ward interception. It appeared they had given it right back to the Titans when Harold Fannin Jr. was stripped by the Titans' Anthony Hill Jr. at the Cleveland 44-yard line.

Just a few yards from scoring range, with a chance to make it a two-score game again, Ward's pick gave the ball right back. The Browns drove for a touchdown to tie the game and, after a Titans three-and-out, Cleveland added a field goal right before the half. It was suddenly 17-14, Cleveland, and Tennessee's momentum was sapped in a brutal second quarter.

The teams played evenly in the second half, although a missed field goal by the Browns was a big boost to the Titans. Either way, the Titans blew their chance to steal a game with that key second-quarter sequence that went the Browns' way.

5. Taaffe's pick gummed up Jets' comeback chances

A rookie safety sniped a veteran quarterback and helped the Dolphins win their first game of the season. Michael Taaffe's second pick of the season came at a critical juncture of Miami's 28-25 victory to end the team's winless start .

The Dolphins took a 14-7 lead early, but the Jets were driving deep in Miami territory. On first-and-10 from the Jets' 21-yard line, Taafe one-upped veteran QB Geno Smith:

The team traded punts on the next two possessions. On Miami's possession after that, it drove 15 plays and 91 yards for a touchdown before the half to take a shocking 21-7 lead. The march soaked up nearly nine minutes, with Jets head coach Aaron Glenn failing to leave any reasonable time back for his offense to score before halftime.

The Jets scored 17 points in the second half, showing some life, but a missed field-goal try was another killer.

It's hard to win games when teams give away as many points as the Jets did Sunday.

articles.title: Dubious roughing calls on Packers in loss to Lions seem to draw outrage everywhere but Detroit
articles.summary: Micah Parsons and Tom Brady were among the vocal critics of the officiating from Sunday's Packers-Lions game.
articles.body:
The Lions beat the Packers on Sunday in a game that moved Green Bay to 4-3, which is good for last place in the NFC North, a half-game behind 4-2 Detroit.

The Lions got some help from officials along the way.

The 20-17 Detroit win was a tight battle down the stretch that featured some dubious roughing-the-passer calls that did not go Green Bay's way. For a game with these stakes attached, there was plenty of noise around those calls — almost all of it slamming officials for how they called the game.

There were two roughing calls against Green Bay that stood out. The first took place with 4:06 remaining in the third quarter and Detroit holding a 17-14 lead.

Lions quarterback Jared Goff threw an incomplete pass on third-and-10 that appeared to set up a Detroit punt. But Packers linebacker Brenton Cox Jr. got called for a soft roughing-the-passer call that Fox play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt called "a gift."

Cox barely touched Goff's torso with two hands as he fell to the turf. Goff responded with a dramatic sell job, falling back on his backside with his legs in the air.

Upon replay, Tom Brady called it "not much at all." Fox officiating analyst Dean Blandino said "I don't like it as roughing."

But the call was the call, and it gave the Lions a first down when they would have otherwise been punting from their own 48. Detroit ran eight more plays from there to the Green Bay 6-yard line before the drive stalled out with a failed fourth-and-5 conversion.

Another roughing call helps set up game-winning FG

The next questionable roughing call arrived with 2:40 remaining and the game locked in a 17-17 tie.

This time, Goff completed a pass for a first down to tight end Sam LaPorta on second-and-8. Defensive tackle Karl Brooks hit Goff just as the QB released the ball.

He didn't hit Goff low. He didn't hit him high. He didn't hit him late. He didn't drive his body weight into Goff.

"My goodness, what is that?" Brady proclaimed. "… That's definitely not roughing the passer."

Blandino described the play as a "teach-tape tackle."

A penalty was called nonetheless. Instead of an 18-yard gain to the Detroit 45, the play pushed the Lions to the Packers' 40. The Lions drove to the Packers' 4-yard line and for a game-winning field goal by Jake Bates as time expired.

Would Detroit have driven for the game-winning field goal without that late roughing call? We'll never know. But we can say with certainty that the call worked in Detroit's favor.

All-Pro Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons remained sidelined for Sunday's game as he continues to recover from surgery to repair a torn ACL last season. But he was watching and shared his thoughts on the officiating on social media.

"Let's just go to flag football if everytime a qb gets touched it's roughing the passer!" Parsons wrote while tagging the NFL and NFL officiating.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was visibly upset during the game. He bit his tongue when asked about the calls in his postgame news conference.

"I don't even want to comment on any of the penalties," he said. "I just — it is what it is. You've gotta play above it.

"I thought there were some some tough calls, but it is what it is."

Packers safety Xavier McKinney, however, did not bite his tongue.

"I would rather get fined and try to help my team out because I see what's going on, and I see that it's killing us," McKinney said. "We all see it. We all see what's going on. Everybody see's what's going on, the fans see what's going on. … You're not even reviewing what you're calling. …

"Even they're looking at it, like, OK that's not it. I'm asking other refs and they're like, 'Oh, I'm not over there.' It's a lot of s*** that doesn't make sense right there."

In 2024, he also joined former Minnesota Vikings teammate Garrett Bradbury to raise money for the Baller Dream Foundation.Both organizations help young cancer patients. articles.title: Broncos' Sean Payton Apologizes for 'Dumb' Reverse Play Call That Led to Jaylen Waddle Injury
articles.summary: Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals with an injury, and head coach Sean Payton took the blame for it.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals with an injury, and head coach Sean Payton took the blame for it.

Payton called the reverse play he ran that resulted in Waddle's injury "dumb."

"Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play."

On the aforementioned play, quarterback Bo Nix tried to flip the ball to Waddle in the backfield, but Waddle couldn't bring the ball in and had to jump on it to avoid losing the fumble. It resulted in a chest injury, and he did not return to the game.

It's hard to blame Payton for wanting to get creative since the Broncos were up big with just a few minutes remaining, but it ultimately led to an injury to one of the key members of his offense.

The severity of Waddle's injury is still not known, but Payton will only be kicking himself more if he's looking at a lengthy return.

Waddle, a sixth-year veteran who joined the Broncos this offseason after five years with the Miami Dolphins, has been Bo Nix's favorite target so far this season, recording 26 receptions for 276 yards and a touchdown. He had four receptions for 48 yards in the 30-16 win on Sunday.

Amid a 5-2 start to the year, Waddle has been a major reason for the team's success. The question now is whether Payton's creative play will cost him any time.

Denver has a tough matchup on deck against the Kansas City Chiefs, and it would prefer to have Waddle available for that divisional game.

articles.title: Dak Prescott for Justin Herbert? Former NFL MVP floats a blockbuster Cowboys-Chargers quarterback swap
articles.summary: Former NFL MVP Boomer Esiason has floated an unlikely quarterback swap that would send Justin Herbert to the Dallas Cowboys and Dak Prescott to the Los
articles.body: Former NFL MVP Boomer Esiason has floated an unlikely quarterback swap that would send Justin Herbert to the Dallas Cowboys and Dak Prescott to the Los Angeles Chargers. The proposal comes as both teams struggle through a disappointing 2026 season, with the Chargers winless at 0-6 and Dallas sitting at 2-4 heading into Week 7. Esiason acknowledged that the deal is unlikely, but his suggestion has raised a bigger question: would changing quarterbacks solve either team's problems, or would it simply shift the pressure to a new player?Boomer Esiason pitches a Prescott-Herbert swapEsiason shared the idea on *Kickoff with Boomer and Valenti* after a discussion about whether the Cowboys should consider moving on from Prescott. Rather than simply suggest a new direction for Dallas, the former Cincinnati Bengals quarterback proposed an exchange that would send both established starters to the other franchise."Did you see Justin Herbert wearing a Dallas Cowboys uniform? Let's just fantasize about that for a second. I can see it. I mean, Justin Herbert goes to the Cowboys and Dak Prescott goes to the Chargers. That would be amazing. That would be great for NFL. That would be great for football," Esiason said.He also recognised the practical barriers. Both quarterbacks may have no-trade clauses in their contracts, and any deal would require the teams and players to agree. Esiason suggested that frustration with their current situations could make the idea more appealing by the end of the season, but he stopped short of predicting a move."So I think that would be a dream scenario for all of us who cover the NFL. I don't know that would help. And I don't think Dak is going anywhere."That final point undercuts the blockbuster appeal. Prescott remains an established figure in Dallas, and a rough stretch does not automatically mean the Cowboys are ready to give up on him. The proposal is an intriguing talking point, not evidence of active trade discussions.Why the trade would not fix everythingHerbert's age is one of the clearest differences between the two quarterbacks. At 28, he is five years younger than the 33-year-old Prescott. That could make Herbert more attractive to a Dallas team thinking about its longer-term future, particularly if it believes a different supporting cast could help him reach another level.His 2026 numbers, however, have raised concerns. Through six games, Herbert has completed 59.4% of his passes for five touchdowns and eight interceptions. Prescott has completed 66.3% of his attempts, with 1,639 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. Those figures give Dallas the stronger statistical case at quarterback so far, even as the Cowboys struggle to win consistently.The larger issue is whether either team would benefit from the exchange. Herbert has struggled to deliver sustained playoff success, while Prescott has faced years of scrutiny over Dallas' postseason results. A new uniform might change the conversation, but it would not guarantee better protection, stronger defensive play or a deeper playoff run.For the Chargers, trading away a younger franchise quarterback for an older one would be a major decision. For Dallas, replacing a familiar leader with Herbert would carry its own risks. Esiason's proposal offers a fascinating hypothetical, but both teams would need far more than a quarterback swap to turn their seasons around.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers retirement stance takes a twist as the Pittsburgh Steelers QB sticks to his final season plan amid breaking Peyton Manning’s NFL record
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers gave Pittsburgh Steelers fans another reason to celebrate.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers gave Pittsburgh Steelers fans another reason to celebrate. He passed Peyton Manning on the NFL’s all-time regular-season passing touchdown list during a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris. But the record-breaking moment did not change his mind about retirement. Rodgers has already said the 2026 NFL season will be his last, and he made it clear after the game that he has no plans to return for another year.The 42-year-old quarterback has enjoyed a strong run with Pittsburgh in recent weeks. His latest milestone added another achievement to his Hall of Fame career. Still, fans hoping the victory might convince him to stay longer got a firm answer. Rodgers wants to finish his NFL career this season and spend more time with his growing family. Aaron Rodgers shuts down retirement u-turn after Steelers’ win in ParisA reporter asked Rodgers about playing another season during his postgame press conference in Paris. The question came after his memorable touchdown pass to tight end Darnell Washington helped Pittsburgh take control against New Orleans.Rodgers did not leave much room for debate.“No, no, no,” the Steelers quarterback replied when asked if the reporter could convince him to play one more year.He also spoke about enjoying the NFL’s international games. Rodgers played in London in 2022 and 2024 before facing the Saints in France. He explained that Green Bay rarely played overseas because of Lambeau Field’s home-field advantage.“I’ve enjoyed the last two especially international games,” Rodgers said during the Paris postgame press conference.His comments followed a retirement announcement he made on May 20, 2026. During a news conference at the Steelers’ organized team activities in Pittsburgh, Rodgers confirmed that this season would mark the end of his NFL career.“Yes. This is it,” he told reporters when asked if 2026 would be his final season.The decision came after Mike Tomlin stepped down as Pittsburgh’s head coach following the Steelers’ playoff loss to the Houston Texans in January. Rodgers had considered walking away, but the team’s decision to hire Mike McCarthy changed his thinking.Rodgers spent 13 seasons playing under McCarthy with the Green Bay Packers. They won Super Bowl XLV together, giving the quarterback another reason to return for one final season. Why Aaron Rodgers wants to leave the NFL after the 2026 seasonRodgers has also started thinking about life after football. During an appearance on Mad Dog Sports Radio with Adam Schein, he discussed his plans to support his pregnant wife and begin a new chapter away from the spotlight.“I’m hopefully gonna be supporting my pregnant wife, because we’re gonna start a family,” Rodgers said on the radio show. “And I am not gonna be making a lot of appearances or statements, and I’m looking forward to a life of quiet after 23 years in the pros and three in college.”For now, though, Rodgers still has football to play. His 2025 season with Pittsburgh brought 3,322 passing yards and 24 touchdowns across 16 games. He also took 29 sacks, showing the physical demands that come with playing late into his career.Against the Saints on October 25, Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 217 yards and one touchdown without an interception. His four-yard scoring pass to Washington gave him 540 career regular-season touchdown passes, moving him past Manning’s 539.Only Drew Brees, with 571, and Tom Brady, with 649, now sit ahead of Rodgers on the list.The record adds another major achievement to his final NFL season. The Las Vegas Raiders are currently mired in a four-game losing streak, and the elephant in the room is when the team might consider replacing veteran Kirk Cousins with 2026 top overall pick Fernando Mendoza at quarterback.

If the switch becomes necessary, Cousins seems prepared to accept it gracefully.

"It's really the same every day that it was in March or April. articles.title: “I'm just happy that I've been able to influence”:  How Travis Kelce used a fashion show to support Kansas City kids before becoming NFL superstar
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has spent years making plays for the Kansas City Chiefs, but his work off the field started taking shape early in his NFL career.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent years making plays for the Kansas City Chiefs, but his work off the field started taking shape early in his NFL career. In April 2016, the tight end came up with a different way to support children in Kansas City. He organised a fashion show that brought local models, children and his teammates together for a charity event. The idea was simple, but Kelce wanted to do more than just show up and lend his name to a cause.The event, called the Walk the Walk Fashion Benefit, took place at Tom's Town Distillery in downtown Kansas City. It supported Shadow Buddies and Operation Breakthrough, two organisations Kelce had already started working with. His nonprofit, Eighty-Seven & Running, also benefited from the event, according to Shadow Buddies Foundation. For a player still building his NFL career, it was an early example of how he wanted to use his growing platform to help his community.How Travis Kelce turned a fashion show into a charity event for Kansas City kidsThe Walk the Walk Fashion Benefit took place on April 6, 2016. Kelce developed the idea himself, bringing Kansas City fashion into a fundraising event with a purpose beyond the runway.Children from Operation Breakthrough joined local models to walk the runway, while guests enjoyed food, drinks and a private shopping experience. The event also drew local personalities and Kelce's Chiefs teammates James O'Shaughnessy, Brian Parker and Ross Travis. Tight ends coach Tom Melvin attended as well.Kelce explained his thinking in an interview published on the Kansas City Chiefs' official website on April 8, 2016."I wanted it to be something fun, something interactive," he said. "It's all for a great cause. I'm just happy that I've been able to influence this city and be a part of it. The city has brought me in as one of its own, and I just feel like this is my opportunity to give back and when I can, make a great influence."Kelce wanted to use his standing in Kansas City to bring people together and support organisations working with children.The proceeds went to Shadow Buddies and Operation Breakthrough, along with Kelce's Eighty-Seven & Running nonprofit. However, the available accounts do not disclose the total amount raised, so there is no confirmed figure to attach to the fundraiser.Why Shadow Buddies and Operation Breakthrough were part of Travis Kelce's planKelce's choice of beneficiaries was not random. Both organisations had supported his charitable mission, and he wanted to help them reach more people."[Shadow Buddies and Operation Breakthrough] were the first two that really got on board to what my mission was and what I wanted to be a part of," Kelce told the Chiefs' official website in the April 8, 2016 interview.He added, "Both Shadow Buddies and Operation Breakthrough have been awesome for me, for this community and for the surrounding communities. It's awesome just to be a part of them and be a face for them and they can be a face for me."Shadow Buddies creates doll-like companions that help children and families cope with illness and medical experiences. Operation Breakthrough works with children and families in Kansas City, providing educational and support services.There was also a connection to Chiefs history. Former Kansas City tight end Tony Gonzalez had helped establish the Shadow Buddies programme in the city, and Kelce continued that tradition through his involvement.The fashion benefit gave Kelce a chance to support both organisations while bringing his teammates and the wider community into the effort. He even joined the runway himself, dancing and skipping as guests cheered him on.Today, Kelce is known worldwide for his NFL career, but the 2016 event offers a look at an earlier side of the Chiefs star. With the 12th Man behind them, Seattle entered the matchup as a 3-point favorite over Kansas City, according to FanDuelSportsbook .

It was an ugly game for the Chiefs' offense, with dropped passes, turnovers, and missed opportunities at every turn.

Mahomes was held without a touchdown, marking back-to-back games in which the former two-time NFL MVP failed to find the end zone.

Not only was Mahomes held without a touchdown, but Kansas City failed to reach the red zone all game, marking the first time in Mahomes' career that the Chiefs were held out of the red zone.

The Chiefs fell to 5-1 on the season, while Seattle snapped a two-game losing streak to improve to 4-3.

With the Chiefs' loss and the San Francisco 49ers falling earlier Sunday, the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings are the only undefeated team remaining in the 2026 NFL season.

After a scoreless first quarter, the Seahawks took a 10-0 lead into halftime behind a field goal and a 28-yard touchdown pass from Darnold to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Darnold threw an interception before halftime, but Kansas City's Harrison Butker missed a 58-yard field goal on the ensuing possession, negating the turnover.

Meanwhile, Mahomes and the Chiefs struggled offensively, punting on three possessions and throwing an interception as they entered halftime without a point and just 92 total yards of offense.

Both teams added field goals in the third quarter, with Butker nailing a 50-yarder to put the Chiefs on the board for the first time with 1:42 remaining in the quarter.

With a chance to cut the deficit to one score, Butker missed his second field goal of the game, giving the ball back to Seattle.

The Seahawks ran down the clock and capped the drive with a 21-yard rushing touchdown by Emanuel Wilson to extend their lead, before sealing the win with a defensive stop on downs.

The Chiefs will remain on the road to face the Denver Broncos next Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, while the Seahawks will take on the Chicago Bears next Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Seattle Seahawks dominate Chiefs 20-3 as Sam Darnold silences critics in potential Super Bowl preview
articles.summary: Sam Darnold and Jaxson Smith-Njigba lead Seattle offense as the Seahawks dominated the Kansas City Chiefs in a surprising Sunday night blowout.
articles.body: After a bizarre 2025 season, the Kansas City Chiefs are right back at the top of the NFL in 2026 and already well on their way toward yet another Chiefs-Bills AFC Championship game. But last year's Super Bowl Champions, the Seattle Seahawks, have been far less convincing. The surprising loss to the Commanders was followed by a win over the hapless LA Chargers, then two frustrating losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos in overtime. Last weekend's loss was ugly enough that speculation started immediately afterward that Sam Darnold might be in danger of losing his starting job to Drew Lock. From Super Bowl winner to backing up Drew Lock in six games? It sounds crazy, but that's what going 27/51 with no touchdowns and two interceptions, in a losing effort to a quarterback with 107 passing yards, does in the NFL. "There's other times he needs to take care of the football, but I think these are solutions we can find with Sam as our QB. I believe that." "I think we have a lot of faith in Sam," he added in a news conference that same day. "Sam’s played great football for us. He’s done a lot of great things this year. We’ve obviously turned the ball over more than we want to. I feel like there’s things on our end that can help him play better football. And I think he’s definitely part of the solution, rather than the opposite." He, and Seahawks fans, are probably glad Macdonald stuck with him. Despite some further, back-breaking struggles with ball security. After a punt-filled first quarter, the second provided a lot more action. After yet another big 28-yard completion to Smith-Njigba to put the ball at the Kansas City 2-yard-line with 30 seconds left in the half, the Seahawks tried a George Holani run that went backwards. articles.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Says His 'Eyes Get Big' When Facing Man Coverage After 150-Yard Game vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks spoiled the Kansas City Chiefs' perfect record on Sunday with a dominant 20-3 win.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks spoiled the Kansas City Chiefs' perfect record on Sunday with a dominant 20-3 win.

Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba said that, despite it being relatively early in the season, his team treated the matchup like a playoff game.

"Our backs were against the wall and just how we came out here as a brotherhood and fought and swung," Smith-Njigba said. "The resiliency of our team is something special, and we're going to keep doing it."

Contenders starting to separate themselves after Week 7

Smith-Njigba led the way for his team with 150 receiving yards and a touchdown, completely torching the Chiefs' man coverage against him.

"Eyes get big when I see it," Smith-Njigba said of man coverage from the Chiefs. "I know that if we got the chance to take a shot in man coverage, so always love my chances when I see that."

articles.title: Seahawks defense dominates Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III in big win
articles.summary: Seattle’s elite defense held Kansas City to its fewest total yards, first downs and red zone drives in any Mahomes start.
articles.body: The Kenneth Walker III revenge game didn’t go as planned. The Seattle Seahawks’ defense dominated in a 20-3 win over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in a Sunday nightcap, holding Patrick Mahomes and Walker, who won Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks in February — to their lowest passing and rushing totals of the season, respectively. After having lost two straight games, Seattle got its best win of the season and is now only two games behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West. “Really proud of our team,” Seahawks coach Mike MacDonald said postgame. “To stand steadfast in some adversity, that’s what we do. We find solutions.” The Seahawks’ defense was the story. Mahomes was limited to only 165 yards through the air. He threw for no touchdowns and one interception. Meanwhile, Walker was limited even further. He entered Sunday’s game leading the NFL in rushing yards and yards per carry (minimum 30 carries) and tied for the third-most rushing touchdowns. Against his former team, Walker ran only 14 times for 36 yards and no scores. He had run for at least 115 yards in four of the Chiefs’ first five games, and his previous lowest rushing total of the season was 70. Walker walked off the field after the loss without greeting his former teammates. The Seahawks ultimately held Kansas City to its fewest total yards, first downs and red-zone drives in any Mahomes start, while the Chiefs’ three points were also tied for their lowest output in any Mahomes start, per NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno. “Our guys played great, man,” MacDonald said when he was asked about his defense. “They’re just a bunch of warriors.” He added: “How do you not just tip your cap to those guys?” Said Chiefs coach Andy Reid about his offense: “We’ll go back to the drawing board.” The win was a much-needed breakthrough for Seattle, which has had an up-and-down season in defense of its Super Bowl win. The Seahawks won their first two games before they dropped three out of their last four. Their losses have been close, though, as all three came by a combined eight points. Kansas City’s three points were the fewest by a Seattle opponent this season. And on the other side of the ball, quarterback Sam Darnold had one of his better performances of the year. After having thrown two interceptions in three out of the last four weeks — all in losses — Darnold threw for 257 yards, one touchdown and only one pick Sunday night. He was aided greatly by receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had nine catches for 150 yards and a score. And in an ironic twist, the Seahawks had one of their best rushing performances of the season. Seattle ran the ball 41 times for 153 yards, its second-highest total on the ground this season. Running back Emanuel Wilson ran for 100 yards, the first time a Seahawks player has reached the century mark since Walker did it in the Super Bowl. Seattle is now 4-3 with two straight home games over the next two weeks. The Chiefs fell to 5-1, scoring fewer than 22 points for the first time this year. Mahomes never looked in sync, while his receivers failed to create separation against one of the league’s best secondaries. Of Mahomes’ 19 completions, 11 went to Walker and tight ends. “You gotta feel it. This sucks,” Mahomes said of the overall performance. Kicker Harrison Butker didn’t help the cause, missing two field-goal attempts, one of which would have made it a 13-6 game in the fourth quarter. “All three phases, we gotta do better,” Reid said. “I take full responsibility for this.” Kansas City’s offense will need to bounce back quickly, as it will face another great defense in the Denver Broncos in Week 8. The Seahawks, meanwhile, will be tested again on Nov. 2 when they host the 5-2 Chicago Bears, who’ve averaged 30.8 points in quarterback Caleb Williams’ four starts.
