articles.title: NFL: Seattle Seahawks hand Kansas City Chiefs first season loss as Jaxon Smith-Njigba stars and Patrick Mahomes struggles
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs stumbled Sunday night against the Seattle Seahawks, losing 20-3 to suffer their first loss of the season; Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III both had quiet nights for the Chiefs (5-1); watch the NFL live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Sam Darnold threw for 257 yards and a score for the Seahawks (4-3), who snapped a two-game losing streak and handed the Chiefs (5-1) their first loss of the season.

Emanuel Wilson also had 24 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown for the Seahawks, who kept Patrick Mahomes and former player Kenneth Walker III quiet during a victory that gets their season back on track.

Mahomes struggled, throwing for 165 yards with an interception while Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks last season before signing with the Chiefs in the offseason, was held to 36 yards on 14 carries.

Walker entered the night averaging a league-leading 133 yards per game, but the Seahawks shut him down - along with the rest of Kansas City's offense - as the Chiefs had 213 total yards, 50 on the ground.

"Listen, all three phases we struggled, so we've got to do better, and that's my responsibility," Kansas City coach Andy Reid said. "So I take full responsibility for this. We've got to play better as a team."

The only bright spot for Kansas City's offense was a milestone for Travis Kelce, who had four receptions to reach 1,104 for his career, moving past Marvin Harrison and Cris Carter for fifth in NFL history .

How Seahawks ended Chiefs' unbeaten start

After Darnold hit Smith-Njigba for a 33-yard gain early in the second quarter to get the Seahawks in the red zone, Jason Myers kicked a 25-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead.

On the next series, Ty Okada intercepted Mahomes on a pass intended for Jalen Royals. Seattle's ensuing drive was kept alive by Darnold's seven-yard scramble. He then connected with Smith-Njigba for a 28-yard touchdown to put Seattle up 10-0 with 1:44 left in the first half.

Another 28-yard pass from Darnold to Smith-Njigba got the Seahawks to the Kansas City one in the closing seconds of the half, but Darnold was intercepted by Nohl Williams in the back of the end zone. Williams returned the pick 64 yards, but Harrison Butker's 58-yard field goal attempt fell short as time expired.

Myers made a 35-yard field goal to extend Seattle's lead to 13-0. Before the third quarter was over, the Chiefs drove to the Seattle 30, but Mahomes fumbled on third down and Kansas City had to settle for Butker's 50-yard field goal.

Mahomes found Kelce for a 19-yard catch early in the fourth quarter, but the Chiefs came away with no points when Butker missed a 45-yard field goal attempt wide right. Butker has missed 10 field goals since the start of last season.

The Seahawks pushed their lead to 20-3 on Wilson's 21-yard scoring run with 3:47 left.

"I think this game reminds the guys what we're capable of," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. "I think our guys understand that there's more levels to where we can go, and so I hope they feel the sense of urgency that we can get there because it is stuff that we can control."

articles.title: NFL: Minnesota Vikings are last unbeaten team after Kansas City Chiefs lose
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers lost in week seven of the NFL, leaving the Minnesota Vikings as this season's last unbeaten team.
articles.body:
Week seven of the NFL left one unbeaten team standing and few - if any - would have picked them out at the start of the season.

The Kansas City Chiefs were beaten at defending champions the Seattle Seahawks while the San Francisco 49ers also suffered their first loss.

But the Minnesota Vikings marched on to maintain their 100% record, and there were also big wins for the Cleveland Browns and Denver Broncos.

Here are the biggest stories from Sunday's games in the NFL.

Kansas City and Seattle have not only won three of the past four Super Bowls, they came into week seven with this season's best offence and best defence respectively, in terms of total yards.

Sunday's primetime match also marked the return of Kenneth Walker, the Most Valuable Player in last season's Super Bowl, to former team Seattle after joining the Chiefs in the off-season.

The running back has made a stunning start with Kansas City, leading the NFL in rushing yards per game (133) after six weeks, but Seattle's defence was determined to show why they became known as 'the Dark Side' during last season's championship run.

They stifled Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs, restricting Walker to 36 yards from 14 carries as KC tied for their fewest points in a game with Mahomes as their starting quarterback.

Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold also continued to lean on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, with last season's offensive player of the year claiming 150 receiving yards and a touchdown, while new running back Emanuel Wilson finished with 100 rushing yards and a score.

The Seahawks ran out 20-3 winners to improve their record to 4-3, while the Chiefs are now 5-1.

Brock Purdy went to the top of the all-time list for career passer rating last week but did not hit his normal high standards as the San Francisco quarterback was frustrated by the Atlanta Falcons.

The hosts forced four turnovers, including two Purdy interceptions, as they won 29-20 to inflict a first loss on the new Super Bowl favourites.

The 49ers are 6-1 while NFC West rivals the Los Angeles Rams - the pre-season favourites - got back to winning ways.

The Rams are 3-4 after winning 35-21 at the Las Vegas Raiders, where Matt Stafford became the first player to lead two teams for touchdown passes.

Last season's MVP previously set the franchise record for the Detroit Lions before joining the Rams in 2021.

They next face the Los Angeles Chargers, who are the last remaining winless team after the Miami Dolphins won 28-25 at the New York Jets.

For the first time in the NFL, two divisions will go into week eight with all four teams having a record better than 50%.

One of those is the NFC North, topped by the Minnesota Vikings. Before the season, half the NFL was considered to have a better chance of winning the Super Bowl.

But they are the last undefeated team at 6-0 after coming from behind to win 16-10 at home to the Indianapolis Colts.

Their defence has been one of the league's best, Will Reichard is yet to miss a kick and - although their offence is yet to catch fire - the Vikings keep grinding out victories.

Including the end of last season, Kevin O'Connell's team are on an 11-game win streak, but they face a test at divisional rivals Detroit next week.

After naming new signing Kyler Murray as their starting quarterback, the Vikings traded JJ McCarthy four weeks ago and he impressed on his first start for the New York Giants on Sunday, leading them to a 27-21 win in overtime at the Houston Texans.

Elsewhere in the NFC North, Jessie Bates kicked a field goal as time expired to hand the Detroit Lions a 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers.

Only three field-goal attempts have been missed from inside 35 yards all season and Green Bay rookie Trey Smack missed two of them on Sunday.

All AFC North teams also have at least four wins, with the Pittsburgh Steelers kicking off Sunday's action by beating the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the NFL's first game in France.

The Cleveland Browns (5-2) then regained top spot after Andre Szmyt made his third game-winning kick in four weeks to claim a 27-24 win at the Tennessee Titans.

Deshaun Watson was booed by Cleveland fans in pre-season but has now led five game-winning drives this season and is beginning to look like the player he was at Houston, which convinced the Browns to sign him on a fully-guaranteed deal in 2022 worth $230m (£172m).

Their other divisional rivals went head-to-head. The Baltimore Ravens had to manage without quarterback Lamar Jackson for a third straight game and led the Cincinnati Bengals 13-0 at half-time.

But the Bengals stormed back to win 35-13, with Joe Burrow throwing for four touchdowns and 292 yards as the Ravens suffered a second straight loss.

Baltimore have not set a return date for two-time MVP Jackson (ankle) and have a tough trip to the Buffalo Bills next week.

Titans release Elliott for pulling gun in car park

The Denver Broncos earned the top seed in the AFC Conference last season but, although they beat Buffalo in the divisional round, the win was overshadowed by a late injury to Bo Nix.

A broken ankle meant the Broncos had to do without their starting quarterback the following week as the New England Patriots denied them a spot in the Super Bowl.

Over their first six games of the season, some questioned whether two off-season surgeries had impacted on his ability to run the ball, which had been a valuable weapon for Denver. Nix had also struggled with his arm.

But the third-year quarterback responded in style, rushing for a 62-yard touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals - the longest QB run since 2022.

Nix finished with 222 passing yards and a touchdown pass as the Broncos won 30-16 to go 5-2 in the AFC West behind Kansas City, who they host next week.

articles.title: Commanders' big picture analysis through seven weeks
articles.summary: Here are some things we've noticed through Washington's first six games.
articles.body:
With the Washington Commanders ' bye week just concluded, what are some big-picture observations of the team's first six games?

Both offensive and defensive coordinators are in their first year at this elevated position in the NFL. That has shown at various times. The defense surrendered huge, explosive plays in both of Washington's first two losses. Then they couldn't stop the Colts ' running game in the second half (Week 4), blew a 14-point fourth-quarter lead against the Giants (Week 5), and offered little resistance to the 49ers' first-half attack (Week 6). Offensively, the biggest Achilles' heel thus far has been penalties, most notably pre-snap penalties. And of course the clock management against the Giants was disturbing, and the offense was anemic in the first half against the 49ers.

Head coach Dan Quinn has been the subject of much speculation over the last two weeks. Some in the national media called for him to lose his job during the bye week. One even called for him "to do the honorable thing and resign" after the fiasco of the conclusion of the Giants 27-27 tie.

We now know that as early as training camp, Quinn and DC Daronte Jones were already discussing bringing on an additional set of eyes as a consultant. Perhaps Quinn (or Jones) realized then that they wanted to add someone with more experience to the defensive staff.

The NFC East is, without question, the weakest division in the NFL this season. This is confirmed by the fact that in Weeks 5 and 6, no NFC East team managed a single win. The Eagles and Cowboys play Monday night; the winner will be 3-4, and the loser will fall to 2-5. The Commanders are currently 1-4-1.

The Commanders have lost two receivers already in the first six games. Losing Terry McLaurin will continue to limit the Commanders the rest of the way. Jaylen Lane, remember, returned two punts for touchdowns in 2025. No one has yet shown explosiveness like Lane in the return game. Dyami Brown has to produce more down the field or defenses are going to play up and press at the line of scrimmage.

Some aspects of the offense are troubling. Washington's run block rate is at or near the bottom after each week. Then they lost Bill Croskey-Merritt, the only running back who has exhibited any ability to produce a big play. Losing LT Laremy Tunsil no doubt limits the offense. And what is the deal with Rachaad White looking like he doesn't know the playbook? Jayden Daniels has been correcting White several times in the last two games.

The 2024 draft class, Adam Peters' first draft class, has disappointed often. They have underperformed; they have not been productive. I didn't want to jump on that class prematurely like others did last season, but this is their third season, and it raises questions about that class. LB Jordan Magee hasn't been able to stay on the field, WR Luke McCaffrey has been called upon far less this season, TE Ben Sinnott simply hasn't developed, and CB Mike Sainristill has regressed so much that his playing time has been dramatically reduced. OL Brandon Coleman has filled in admirably for Tunsil, yet really struggled a few times as well.

QB Jayden Daniels: We are not simply creating a narrative, was one DC radio station personality accused this week. No, Daniels has made glaring mental mistakes in the last two games; how can an experienced observer for years not be alarmed? His situational awareness was lacking in crucial moments in each of the last two games. He clearly (no overstatement) needs better coaching on those types of game scenarios involving down & distance, as well as clock management. He has played well when he's been on the field, though.

Dan Quinn is in trouble. I am one of the last to come to the conclusion, because I like Quinn as a person, a motivator, and an encourager. But coaches are hired to produce wins, and they aren't. I am certainly hoping the Commanders can make a second-half run to win the division. However, the team would need to go 7-5 in the last 12 games to simply avoid a losing season (8-8-1). They are two full games behind the Giants (4-2-1) and thus may need at the least an 8-4 finish to have a chance at the NFC East. Here's to hoping Dan Quinn can lead the players and coaches through these last 12 weeks to a successful finish and a playoff berth.

articles.title: Micah Parsons snaps at NFL’s officiating after Packers’ three-point loss vs. Lions
articles.summary: Micah Parsons has taken aim at NFL officials after the Green Bay Packers suffered a narrow 20-17 defeat to the Detroit Lions, with a controversial roughing t...
articles.body:
Micah Parsons has taken aim at NFL officials after the Green Bay Packers suffered a narrow 20-17 defeat to the Detroit Lions, with a controversial roughing the passer penalty becoming a major talking point.

The Lions secured victory with a last-second field goal from Jake Bates, but the officiating attracted plenty of attention following two disputed penalties against Green Bay.

Parsons was watching from the sidelines as he continues to recover from a torn ACL, but that did not stop the Packers' pass rusher from making his feelings clear on social media.

Micah Parsons questions NFL's roughing the passer calls

Parsons shared his frustration on X, tagging both the NFL and its officiating account after officials penalised Packers defensive lineman Karl Brooks for roughing the passer late in the fourth quarter.

He wrote: "@NFL, @NFLOfficiating let's just go to flag football if every time a QB gets touched it's roughing the passer!"

The call came after Brooks made contact with Lions quarterback Jared Goff following an 18-yard completion to tight end Sam LaPorta. The 15-yard penalty helped Detroit continue its drive before Bates delivered the winning field goal.

Former NFL quarterback Tom Brady also questioned the decision while working as a Fox Sports analyst.

"My goodness. What is that?" Brady said during the broadcast. "There's no way!"

Fox rules analyst Dean Blandino also backed the criticism, saying: "That's teach-tape tackle. That's not roughing the passer."

It was not the only disputed decision, with Packers defender Brenton Cox Jr. also penalised for roughing Goff earlier in the contest.

Parsons could face a fine for publicly criticising the officiating, according to reports, although no punishment had been confirmed. A suspension is considered unlikely.

Green Bay also had opportunities to win the game, with two missed field goals from Trey Smack and a crucial fourth-quarter interception thrown by Jordan Love contributing to the defeat.

Parsons has now missed seven consecutive games while recovering from his ACL injury, leaving the Packers to wait for his return as the debate over the officials' decisions continues.

articles.title: ‘Cris Collinsworth Is So Unbelievably Cringeworthy,’ ‘Crazy’ — NFL Fans Rip NBC Broadcaster for ‘Glazing’ Patrick Mahomes After a Fumble
articles.summary: NBC analyst Cris Collinsworth showering Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes with over-the-top praise is nothing new. At this point, it has practic...
articles.body:
NBC analyst Cris Collinsworth showering Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes with over-the-top praise is nothing new. At this point, it has practically become a tradition during NFL broadcasts. Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks was no different.

The Chiefs struggled to get anything going offensively and fell 20-3 to the reigning Super Bowl champions, but Collinsworth still found a moment to gush over Mahomes. It didn't take long for fans to notice, and the clip quickly made the rounds on social media.

Cris Collinsworth Takes Heat for His Boundless Praise of Patrick Mahomes

The moment came in the third quarter, when Mahomes scrambled, took a hit, and fumbled the ball. The Chiefs quarterback then dove back into the pile and managed to recover it himself.

Watching the replay, Collinsworth couldn't help himself, saying, "What other quarterback is getting up twice to go get this football?"

Collinsworth wasn't done defending Mahomes, either. As the Chiefs' offensive struggles continued, the NBC analyst turned his attention to the quarterback's body language.

"That's the second time I've seen that look on Patrick Mahomes' face. When he went back and recovered that fumble earlier, I saw that same sort of 'I can't believe this is happening to me' look. There it is again. Have you ever seen that look on Patrick Mahomes?" he asked.

Reacting to these moments, one fan tweeted , "Cris Collinsworth is so unbelievably cringeworthy when it comes to talking about Patrick Mahomes."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Associated Press reporter Rob Maaddi took issue with Collinsworth's original point, arguing that recovering a fumble shouldn't be treated as something extraordinary for a quarterback. "The question should be: Which QB doesn't get up to go after a loose ball because that's what would actually be rare," he wrote .

"Cris Collinsworth glazing Mahomes even after fumbling is crazy," a third fan wrote on X.

"Cris Collinsworth waxing poetic for Patrick Mahomes recovering his own fumble," another fan commented .

One user struggled to wrap his head around the question, saying , "Patrick Mahomes got rocked and fumbled, and Cris Collinsworth somehow turns it into praising Mahomes."

After the loss, the Chiefs are 5-1 on the season and currently rank No. 6 in the league with a PFN Team Impact Score of 80.7.

Kansas City's Week 7 loss came down to several factors. The offense managed just 213 total yards, its lowest output in a regular-season game started by Mahomes.

The Chiefs also failed to convert their first five third-down attempts and finished just 3-of-11 on third down. Mahomes' struggles as a runner and his accuracy issues added to the offensive problems.

Kansas City will look to bounce back against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. The game is scheduled to kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET Sunday, Nov. 1.

articles.title: ‘More Than a Bad Game,’ ‘This Is a Bad Sign’ — Ex-Eagles LB Sounds The Alarm as Chiefs’ Stalled Offense Hits Rock Bottom in Patrick Mahomes Era
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs rolled into Lumen Field on Sunday night unbeaten and averaging an NFL-leading 414 yards a game. They left after scoring a mere three p...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs rolled into Lumen Field on Sunday night unbeaten and averaging an NFL-leading 414 yards a game. They left after scoring a mere three points in their first loss of the season, a 20-3 defeat to the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and a defeat that was a historic low in the Patrick Mahomes era.

However, when former Eagles linebacker Emmanuel Acho broke down the game on his "Speakeasy" show postgame, he pointed to more worrying signs: "It's more than just a bad game for the Chiefs. It's a bad sign."

Emmanuel Acho Points to What Patrick Mahomes' Chiefs Is Missing

Kansas City went into Seattle short-handed at receiver and tackle. Tyquan Thornton, the team's leading receiver, dislocated his ankle in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders and will miss at least three months after surgery.

Rashee Rice has been out since hurting his hamstring in that game. Kansas City was also without starting tackle Jaylon Moore, while Josh Simmons had missed practice earlier in the week because of a back/personal matter.

Acho began with the receivers: "Remember, his top two receivers are out, and one's not coming back in Tyquan Thornton. So Patrick Mahomes is constantly asked to make high-quality lemonade out of limes. You feel me? How are you even going to do that? He's asked to make high-quality lemonade out of limes, and at best, poverty lemons."

Mahomes' longest completion on Sunday went for 19 yards. The Chiefs had piled up nearly 160 rushing yards a game through their first five outings, much of it from Kenneth Walker III, Seattle's Super Bowl MVP last season.

Walker came into Week 7 leading the league at 133 rushing yards a game, and ranking first in PFN's NFL RB Impact Score with his 96.5 grade.

Seattle, which hasn't allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 games, held its former running back to a season-low 36 yards on 14 carries with no run longer than seven yards, and Kansas City finished with 50 rushing yards on 16 carries.

Acho then pointed to the Chiefs' run game: "If you can stop the run game, hard to do, I get it. But if you can stop the run game, now Patrick Mahomes has to rely on Xavier Worthy, who hasn't proven himself to be a bona fide number one, and an older Travis Kelce."

Kelce was held without a catch in the first half and finished with four grabs for 44 yards. That was enough to pass Marvin Harrison and Cris Carter for fifth on the NFL's all-time receptions list.

Acho closed with a warning: "There are a few teams that can do to the Chiefs what the Seahawks did to the Chiefs tonight, about three or so, and when you face those three or so teams, it will be bad."

How the Sunday Night Seahawks Loss Stacks Up in the Patrick Mahomes Era

Several lows in the Chiefs' Mahomes era stood out during their loss to the Seahawks on Sunday night.

The three points tied the fewest Kansas City has scored in a game Mahomes started, matching a 27-3 loss to the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 24, 2021. It was also only the third time in his career that the Chiefs failed to reach double figures.

For the first time in a Mahomes start, Kansas City never reached the red zone. Its 213 yards were the lowest in a regular-season game he started, with only a 212-yard playoff win over the Houston Texans coming in lower.

The Chiefs also went without an explosive play (a run of at least 10 yards or a pass of at least 20) for the first time in Andy Reid's head-coaching career.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Mahomes finished 19 of 33 for 165 yards with no touchdowns, an interception, and a 58.3 passer rating, while Kansas City managed 11 first downs and converted 3 of 11 third downs.

Harrison Butker supplied the only points with a 50-yard field goal. But he came up short from 58 as the first half expired, and in the fourth quarter he pushed a 45-yarder wide right that would have made it a one-possession game.

Kansas City is still 5-1 and first in the AFC West, a half-game ahead of the 5-2 Denver Broncos. The Chiefs visit Denver on Sunday, Nov. 1, needing a win to stay top of the division.

articles.title: ‘Have to’ – Klint Kubiak’s honest answer on Fernando Mendoza replacing Kirk Cousins as Raiders QB1
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but haven’t let him start a game yet. Rather than put that...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but haven't let him start a game yet.

Rather than put that pressure on Mendoza, the Raiders signed and have started Kirk Cousins in every game this season.

Cousins is a veteran who can help Mendoza develop his game in training, and has been trusted to keep the Raiders afloat this season.

Klint Kubiak's honest answer on Fernando Mendoza becoming Raiders QB1

Speaking after the Las Vegas Raiders' 21-35 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, head coach Klint Kubiak was asked whether he will consider starting Fernando Mendoza as QB1.

After what has been an inconsistent 3-4 start, Kubiak is ready to review the game footage and consider all his options, including starting Mendoza.

Kubiak said: "I think we have to go watch the film. At this point, we're thinking about everything – how to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter and personnel scheme. We have got to talk about all of it."

So far, Kirk Cousins has started every game for the Raiders, with Mendoza getting just a few minutes against the New England Patriots late in the Raiders' Week 4 game.

But with the Raiders now hoping to turn their fortunes around and make an unlikely push for the playoffs, they might have to start giving Mendoza more opportunities going forward.

In their loss against the Rams, Cousins threw for 295 yards with two touchdowns. Unfortunately, he was also sacked twice, which allowed the Rams to gain control during the game.

The Raiders see Mendoza as their long-term quarterback and don't want to rush him into a high-pressure environment so early in his career.

This is a strategy other teams have employed with star-level young quarterbacks. Most notably, the Chiefs used this approach with Patrick Mahomes during his rookie year.

But with the Raiders where they are, Kubiak and the rest of the coaching staff will have to consider pulling the trigger on Mendoza early.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 7 Game vs. Titans
articles.summary: Another week, another close-call victory for the Cleveland Browns. Andre Szmyt sealed the deal with a walk-off field goal from 32 yards out to win 27-24.
articles.body:
Another week, another close-call victory for the Cleveland Browns. Andre Szmyt sealed the deal with a walk-off field goal from 32 yards out to win 27-24.

Many of the Browns' wins this season have been driven by their defense, but the offense took center stage this time. Quinshon Judkins, Deshaun Watson, Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion delivered their best performances of the season as Cleveland piled up 491 total yards.

The Titans didn't go down easily, though. They also had a strong offensive showing, with running back Tony Pollard scoring three touchdowns.

Here's a look at how the Browns' key contributors graded out as Cleveland moved to 5-2 on the season.

Watson has come through for Cleveland in the fourth quarter for much of the season. He did it again by leading the Browns' offense on the field-goal drive that sealed the game.

The difference was how well he played in the first half. Watson was dealing for much of the game and had over 200 yards passing in the first half.

Watson didn't have a passing touchdown, but his nine-yard run to put the Browns up 24-17 in the fourth quarter was huge for ensuring they made the most of the red zone trip.

The quarterback delivered good throws to both KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. to give them YAC opportunities. He'll need to build on that reliably to repeat this kind of performance.

Judkins needed a breakout game and he finally got one in Nashville. The Browns leaned more heavily on the under-center running game, and he rewarded them with his best performance of the season.

He showed off good burst and balance on a 30-yard run and found the end zone twice. The second touchdown was the result of some great blocking up front, but the first touchdown featured a slick cut and a broken tackle to get the ball in.

The run game has struggled for most of the season so this was a great confidence game for Judkins and the offensive line.

Sampson made his first appearance since the season opener and quickly made an impact. He had 45 yards on six carries, including a 19-yarder. Sampson's ability to get to the outside and create some explosives was helpful in the Browns' 183-yard rushing day.

Watson played pretty well, but it was KC Concepcion who had the most exciting performance. He turned a few quick screens into chunk plays and finished with 129 yards on eight catches.

He chipped in another 23 yards rushing. He would have had an even bigger day if he hadn't dropped an easy touchdown in the third quarter. Still, that would have just been extra padding to a career day.

There were plenty of Browns who had a great day on offense, but Denzel Boston wasn't one of them. He only caught three of his eight targets for 27 yards with a costly third-down drop that forced a punt.

He didn't cross the defender's face on the slant that led to Deshaun Watson's interception, adding even more frustration to the rookie's afternoon.

Jeudy wasn't asked to do too much, but he had four catches on his four targets for 21 yards.

Fannin has rarely had the opportunity to show off his after-the-catch skills like he did today. He had six catches for 91 yards, with most of that yardage coming after the catch.

Those skills were most on display when he turned a five-yard pass into a 36-yard gain on the final drive to move the offense into field goal range. He does lose a few points for losing a fumble in the second quarter.

Whiteheart wasn't targeted in the passing game, but he had a good afternoon blocking when he was on the field. That helped out as the Browns had their best running performance of the season.

The rookie put together one of his best performances. He was really clean in pass protection and the Browns were able to get the run game going to his side.

Johnson delivered key blocks on Judkins' second touchdown run and his 30-yard gain. He was even able to help form a clean pocket for Watson for much of the afternoon.

Unfortunately, it's hard to overlook three penalty flags. Johnson was flagged once for illegal use of hands to the face and twice for holding. The second holding penalty was declined, but he still needs to cut down on those infractions.

Again, Watson was sacked only once, and Jenkins' work at the pivot was a big reason for that. The Browns consistently picked up Tennessee's pressure, and Jenkins drove the nose tackle out of the running lane on multiple occasions.

The Titans have some talent on the interior, and Barber was able to mostly keep Watson clean.

Howard was again putting together a clean game, but an injury got in the way. He had few clear defeats in the passing game while sealing the edge for a few good Judkins runs.

Unfortunately, his afternoon came to an end early as he left the game in the third quarter with a possible concussion .

Jones replaced the injured Howard and struggled in pass protection, allowing at least two pressures. He also appeared to move early on the final drive, although no false start was called.

This was a rough day for the Browns pass rush in general. Cam Ward was sacked just one time and Verse didn't register a pressure.

Verse's run defense wasn't even as stellar as usual. He gets credit for making a touchdown-saving play on a goal-line carry from Pollard, but overall he fell short of his role.

Again, the Browns pass rush wasn't good enough and McGuire was no exception. He had a hard time getting by the Titans' tackles and his run defense wasn't anything to write home about.

Williams was one of the few defensive linemen who made some notable plays. He tackled Pollard behind the line of scrimmage twice and generated one of the four quarterback hits on the day for the Browns defense.

Graham made his return after missing a few weeks with a knee injury. He didn't even show up in the box score with a tackle, but he was able to generate a few pressures as a pass-rusher.

This wasn't his best performance, but it was good that he was back on the field.

Collins had one of his least productive games. He was able to tackle Pollard for a one-yard loss to get a TFL on the docket, but that was about it. The Titans' offensive line kept him quiet for most of the afternoon.

Huntington was probably the best run defender among the defensive linemen this week. He penetrated the backfield, disrupted several running plays and registered the defense's only sack.

Schwesinger is putting together a great year, but this game wasn't a highlight. He finished with eight total tackles, but there were few splash plays or impact tackles to bolster his grade here.

He was not as downhill on his run fits and was making tackles downfield too often. No tackles for loss and a missed tackle were uncharacteristic for him against a team that leaned heavily on the ground game.

This game was much more friendly for Williams. He's the thumper of the two linebackers and he was the saving grace for the run defense on more than one occasion.

He had 10 total tackles with two of those for losses. However, it's worth noting that he was picked on in coverage a few times.

Ward lost track of a receiver in what appeared to be a coverage breakdown in the fourth quarter. That's a key error.

However, that mistake doesn't completely overshadow a game where he was mostly his dominant self. The interception was picture-perfect coverage on an in-breaker.

Both outside corners got turnovers. Ward had the interception, but Campbell had a violent punch and rip to get the ball out of Carnell Tate's hands. Ronnie Hickman recovered, but it was Campbell who made the play.

Harden gave up some underneath stuff, but he was a willing tackler and didn't have any drastic errors. He left the game in the third quarter with an injury, but was able to return to action in the fourth.

Delpit was shaky in coverage at times, but he made a few plays to make up for it. He was useful as a blitzer with two quarterback hits and came up to make some key tackles against the run.

Hickman had 10 tackles, but the majority of them were downfield after the Titans had already made a big play. He did nothing notable in coverage and wasn't active in the run game either.

McNeil-Warren didn't get a ton of run with just 19 snaps on defense. However, he continued to make the case for more run with a tackle for no gain on Pollard and another tackle for a loss on the running back.

This one was a repeat performance from last week against the Ravens. Bonus points for kicking the game-winner through, but he sent a 43-yarder into the upright at the beginning of the fourth quarter that would have helped.

Bojorquez had a 59-yard boot and pinned the Titans inside their own 20 on one of his three punts. Can't ask him to do much more.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's wife knows things so dire family is on 'Colts transaction watch' expecting trades or firing
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor's wife Ayanna Taylor posted videos suggesting her husband could be traded as the Indianapolis Colts spiral with no GM and no picks.
articles.body: The 2027 NFL offseason has seemingly begun for the Indianapolis Colts and the most stunning part of it is people within the organization understand that's true. That's how things are following a loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans last week, the firing of general Chris Ballard one day later and a follow-up loss to the punchless but somehow undefeated Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. That is definitely the way things are when the wife of the team's biggest star is talking openly about her husband getting traded. SEASON IS ALREADY OVER FOR THESE FOUR NFL TEAMS AFTER WEEK 5, YOU CAN WRITE THEM OFF NOW Yes, you read that right. Jonathan Taylor's wife Ayanna Taylor over the weekend posted two videos on Instagram saying "players that once seemed untouchable," like her husband, "may now be on the table" in potential trades. Want the most depressing part of this for Colts fans? Jonathan Taylor agreed with his wife's videos that make it clear their family is on what she called "a Colts transaction watch." "I think it's been out there already so her adding doesn't really change anything," Taylor said after Sunday's loss. "Everybody's on TikTok these days so we just have to come in to work and focus." MYSTERY TEAM IN MARVIN HARRISON TRADE STEPS FORWARD, AS TEXANS DEMECO RYANS CONFIRMS REUNION WITH CJ STROUD Ayanna Taylor posted about the dire situation facing her husband's team by painting in her second video the truly depressing picture of what's next. "Look at the situation that they put themselves in," she said. "They have a losing record, they just fired their 10-year GM, and they have no draft picks. How are they going to get new leadership to come in when they really have no options for new leadership to transform the team? "Let's think about it: What do you do when you don't have what you need and you don't have the money to pay for it? ... You trade. That's what brings us back to my husband." FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE Taylor, who scored a touchdown and averaged 5.3 yards per rush against the stifling Vikings defense, is obviously a trade chip for interim general manager Ed Dodds. If Dodds can move Taylor, or right defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, or left defensive tackle Grover Stewart or guard Quenton Nelson, or anyone not named Tyler Warren, before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, then it is a good bet he's going to consider it. That, of course, is going to make coach Shane Steichen's life a little tougher. But maybe Steichen should have considered that before his team lost 12 of its last 14 games dating back to last season and is the only one in the NFL to lose to the Titans this season. Besides, Steichen has bigger problems. Bigger problem No. 1: Whether or not to bench quarterback Daniel Jones who has been a bitter disappointment. Jones threw another interception in a key situation on Sunday when the Colts were trying to rally for a go-ahead touchdown. Jones has thrown four touchdown passes and seven interceptions in seven games and he's completing passes at a career-low clip of under 60%. "I have not thought about a quarterback change," Steichen said after the game. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Well, Steichen should be thinking about it and problem No. 2: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put him and Ballard on notice at the end of last year that the expectations for this year would be high. Ballard is gone, so if the current trend continues firing Steichen is the next logical move. Maybe Steichen can survive the looming garage sale of players over the next couple of weeks. But Steichen would be wise to also put himself on "Colts transaction watch." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: "I take full responsibility": Andy Reid’s response to Chiefs’ 20-3 defeat raises questions after Seattle completely stifled Kansas City’s offense
articles.summary: Andy Reid said the loss was on him. The numbers on Sunday night say it was a lot more than that. Seattle beat Kansas City 20-3 at Lumen Field on Oct.
articles.body: Andy Reid said the loss was on him. The numbers on Sunday night say it was a lot more than that. Seattle beat Kansas City 20-3 at Lumen Field on Oct. 25, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season. Patrick Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception. Kenneth Walker III ran for 36. The Chiefs finished with 213 total yards, no touchdowns and two missed field goals. Reid took full responsibility afterward, but he offered few details on what actually broke down, and that gap is what Chiefs fans will chew on this week.Andy Reid takes the blame after Seattle shuts down Kansas City’s offenseAndy Reid did not dodge the question. “All three phases, we struggled,” he told reporters. “So we’ve got to do better, and that’s my responsibility. I take full responsibility for this. We’ve got to play better as a team.” He also tipped his cap to Seattle and called Lumen Field a tough place to play.Specifics were thin. Reid said he could not point to many stats that made sense of the night, other than third downs on both sides of the ball. On Harrison Butker, who missed two field goals, Reid offered this: “He’s off a bit. So, we’ve got to fix that.”The history makes the night look worse. ESPN Insights noted it was the first time in Mahomes’ career that his team went a full game without a drive reaching the red zone. Three points is also the lowest total of his career. Mahomes was back from a season-ending injury, and he finished 19-for-33 with a passer rating of 58.3. With Walker bottled up, the passing game had nothing to lean on.Seattle won the third-down battle and the clockSeattle’s side explains why. The Seahawks converted 11 of 16 third downs, according to ESPN’s Nate Taylor, and by the middle of the third quarter they had held the ball twice as long as Kansas City and run more than twice as many plays. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo sent extra rushers at Sam Darnold. It rarely mattered. Darnold kept finding Jaxon Smith-Njigba.Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV said the plan was simple. “We can play,” Jones said. “We go out there, and that’s our goal: To shut you down, shut your lights out.”Seattle also knew Walker well, because he played there before. “Of course, he’s been here, so we know what type of running back he is, but we don’t allow people to run through our defense. That’s just us.”Reid said the Chiefs have to learn from it, win or lose. “I’ll start with myself, and we’ll work our way through it and make sure that we teach,” he said. He called the locker room great and said it will take care of business. Denver is next. articles.title: Updated Landing Spots for Jonathan Taylor, Brian Thomas Jr. and Khalil Mack amid NFL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Week 7 is almost complete, and we're roughly two weeks away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Week 7 is almost complete, and we're roughly two weeks away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

We've already seen notable players like J.J. McCarthy and Marvin Harrison Jr. change teams via the trade market this season. We'll undoubtedly see more before the deadline arrives at 4 p.m. ET on November 10.

We still don't know who the NFL's top contenders are, and two of the league's last unbeaten teams fell on Sunday. However, we do have an idea of where some of the biggest needs reside and which playoff hopefuls could be eager to make moves at the deadline.

Here, you'll find updated predictions for some of the biggest names who could betraded, based on team needs, recent results, projected roles, and the latest buzz.

Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars are in control of the AFC South with a 42 record. Logic would suggest that they're more likely to be buyers at the deadline than sellers. However, they have a prime trade chip and a potentially expendable piece in wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

The third-year pass-catcher has seen a dip in production since being a rookie Pro Bowler in 2024. He has just nine catches for 105 yards and a touchdown this season, and he was effectively benched during the second half of Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans—Jacksonville was on bye this past week.

According to Adam Schefter of ESPN and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Jags aren't actively looking to trade Thomas, but "teams are expected to ramp up calls closer to the deadline."

If Jaguars GM James Gladstone can get a first-round pick, as the Arizona Cardinals did for Harrison, he'd have to consider dealing Thomas. The San Francisco 49ers would be a terrific landing spot if he's available.

San Francisco suffered its first loss of the season on Sunday, while playing without injured receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel.

Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor is probably the biggest name who has been floating around the pre-deadline rumor mill. The three-time Pro Bowler is 27, but he remains one of the top do-it-all running backs in the NFL.

Taylor is currently tied for the league lead in rushing touchdowns with eight. He has logged 587 rushing yards, 178 receiving yards, and has averaged 4.9 yards per touch.

The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last week, and they fell to 2-5 on Sunday. While they may not be eager to engage in a fire sale, several teams are eager to add Taylor.

According to ESPN's Stephen Holder , "multiple teams" would be open to adding Taylor on the trade market.

While Taylor could help just about any running-back-needy team, the Minnesota Vikings make the most sense. They remain undefeated but have questions at running back after watching Aaron Jones exit Sunday's game with a knee injury .

Minnesota is still trying to settle quarterback Kyler Murray into its offense, and Taylor could help steady the process. According to Schefter, the Vikings have also held prior interest in Taylor.

With the Miami Dolphins winning on Sunday, the Los Angeles Chargers are the last remaining winless team in the NFL. According to Schefter, Los Angeles doesn't want to deal a key player like pass-rusher Khalil Mack, though teams like the Chicago Bears could keep calling about the future Hall of Famer:

At 0-6, the Chargers should be thinking about their future, and moving Mack would make plenty of sense in that context. He's playing on a one-year deal, and he would bring a sizeable return in a trade.

Mack has started all six games for L.A. this season and has recorded 19 tackles, three sacks, five tackles for loss, and 11 quarterback pressures.

Chicago would also be a sensible landing spot for Mack, and not just because he has a history there. The Bears moved to 5-2 with Thursday night's win over the New England Patriots, and their pass rush (19 total sacks) has been more good than great.

*Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: NFL Monday Night Football preview: Cowboys can't afford to lose to this version of the Eagles
articles.summary: The Cowboys and Eagles are both a disappointing 2-4 this season.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have a decent excuse for their 2-4 start. Injuries have hit hard, and now their injured list includes quarterback Jalen Hurts. It's not the only reason the Eagles are struggling, but it's a factor.

The Dallas Cowboys don't really have many excuses for their 2-4 start. They just haven't played well. The defense has been bad most of the season and the offense has had two off games in a row.

The Cowboys and Eagles were expected to compete for the NFC East title but both just want to get back to .500 before the midway point of the season. The two disappointing teams meet up on Monday night, with the loser on its way toward further obscurity this season. Since Week 2, the Cowboys and Eagles are a combined 1-7.

The Eagles are decimated heading into Monday night. Hurts is out and might miss the rest of the season. He'll be replaced by Tanner McKee, who was ineffective in his first start last week. Starting receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out, as is pass rusher Nolan Smith. Offensive tackle Lane Johnson retired a few games into the season. Star running back Saquon Barkley has been out since Week 4 due to a hamstring injury, but could return against Dallas. He's listed as questionable. Anything would help.

The Cowboys' injury report is reasonably clean, but they're slumping. The Cowboys have lost two in a row and scored just 29 points in those two games. Dallas figured out early in the season that its defense, which gave up the most points in the NFL last season, hadn't improved much. The Cowboys still figured to outscore many teams, with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams on offense. When the offense dipped the past two games, it hasn't been pretty.

Nothing has come easy for any NFC East team this season. One of these two division rivals will sink even further in the standings.

No offense to the Eagles, but it is hard to believe they can stay in the NFC East race without Jalen Hurts. A team this talented shouldn't have its season practically over before the end of October, but that appears to be the case for the Eagles. The Cowboys might still be able to salvage their season. Even though the Giants got a nice win at Houston on Sunday to improve to 4-2-1, they are far from unbeatable. If Dallas loses to an Eagles team that is without several key players to fall to 2-5, not only would their season seem over, the criticism would be relentless after Dallas touted itself as a Super Bowl contender this offseason. Dallas needs this one badly.

The Cowboys passing game has been pretty good, but the run game has been much less productive than last season. Dallas was 31st in rushing yards after Week 6. That has affected the offense as a whole.

"Because of the lack of a running game, we're a little bit one-sided and the best way to be on offense as a unit is to have balance," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after last week's loss to the Packers, via ESPN . "So we have to find balance. And again, there's a lot of reasons for that. There's missed blocks, there's bad calls, there's missed runs, there's different things."

Williams is the key figure in the run game. His yards per rush has gone from 4.8 last season to 3.7 so far this season. An effective run game might also help out the defense by keeping the offense on the field. The Eagles have a solid run defense, ranking 13th in yards allowed per carry through six weeks, but Williams and Dallas will have to have some success against it if the offense wants to get back on track.

Well, this MNF game certainly is less attractive than the schedule-makers anticipated back in May. This game was Eagles -3 this offseason, re-opened Eagles -1 on the lookahead line and now is Eagles +4.5 with Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith out, among others for Philadelphia. The Eagles' injury list reads like a CVS receipt, but at least they get to face the Cowboys coming off a disheartening 23-13 loss to Green Bay. This will be the Eagles' fourth straight game as an underdog and the third time already this season that Philadelphia is a home 'dog. If Dak Prescott & Co. can't get right in this game, it's going to a long season in Dallas.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

We have to be ready for surprises as that wacky NFC East closes out Week 7. Here are three fantasy themes to track as the Cowboys and Eagles renew their rivalry.

1. What version of Saquon Barkley do we see? Barkley hasn't played a full game since the end of September and he hasn't scored a touchdown all year. Barkley has less help than normal, running behind a substandard offensive line and tied to an offense missing its quarterback and best receiver. But if Barkley's hamstring is healthy, this is a favorable matchup.

2. What's the runout for the Dallas receivers? We always expect receivers to be the variance position in fantasy, but even with that, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens have posted erratic returns this year. The Philadelphia pass defense has been average.

3. Will a pass catcher step up for the Eagles? With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks unavailable, this is a key issue for Philadelphia. articles.title: 'I Ain't Going to Lie,' Seahawks Star Wanted to Limit Kenneth Walker's Stats in Revenge Game
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs star running back Kenneth Walker III didn't have the revenge game he wanted against his former Seattle Seahawks squad in Sunday night's 20-3 loss.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs star running back Kenneth Walker III didn't have the revenge game he wanted against his former Seattle Seahawks squad in Sunday night's 20-3 loss.

After entering the game with a league-leading 665 rushing yards, Walker was limited to a season-low 36 yards on 14 carries as the Chiefs suffered their first loss of the year. His return to Seattle marked the first time that a Super Bowl MVP played against his former team the following season.

Walker's former Seahawks teammates admitted that it was the team's goal to hold him in check.

"I ain't going to lie, I did," Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori said of wanting to limit Walker's production, per ESPN's Nate Taylor . "I definitely did want to hold him under 100 [yards]. I don't really listen to all the media noise, but that was my motivation. I know a lot of dudes on the defense, that was their motivation, too, to stop him under 100 and play lights out on defense. I think we did that."

Seattle has now gone 36 consecutive games, including the playoffs, without allowing a 100-yard rusher. After the matchup, Walker headed straight to the Chiefs' locker room inside Lumen Field without greeting his former teammates.

"S--t, we lost," Walker said, explaining his decision. "I was frustrated. That's about it. I [saw] them over there celebrating and s--t. That's about it."

The defending champion Seahawks (4-3) will try to keep the momentum going in another primetime matchup in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears (5-2) on Monday Night Football .

articles.summary: Sunday Night Football delivered an easy cash, and now Monday Night Football features Cowboys vs Eagles with Philadelphia's injuries mounting fast.
articles.body: It was a solid Sunday for me in the NFL with a sweat-free cash on Sunday Night Football between the Chiefs and Seahawks. It was potentially one of the most boring games I've ever watched, but it still was an easy cash. That's more important to me than watching a fun game anyway. Tonight we have Monday Night Football as the Cowboys take on the Eagles. My victory lap will stop here because I have been dead wrong about the Dallas Cowboys. They were the team I expected to win this division, and I thought Dak Prescott would be the league's MVP. That doesn't seem to be the case, as the Cowboys are just 2-4 for the season, and they are 1-2 on the road this year. They've suffered some embarrassing losses this season, and need to turn it around quickly if they want to assure themselves of a spot in the postseason. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Cowboys have lost the past two games and three of their past four games. They hosted the Buccaneers with a backup quarterback and got nothing going, losing 24-16. Then they lost to the Packers 23-13 last week. It wasn't a shootout; it wasn't a well-played game. The Philadelphia Eagles won the Super Bowl two years ago, and while you can't really go higher in success, it has been a steep drop since. Last year, the team had issues with their receiver A.J. articles.title: Eagles fans aren’t loving Jeffrey Lurie’s tone-deaf Hall of Fame statement amid Jalen Hurts fiasco
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are embroiled in a controversy after quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs, ending his season. The NFL...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are embroiled in a controversy after quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs, ending his season.

The NFL has been urged to investigate the Eagles' potential culpability in Hurts' terrible setback, especially after the team cleared him to play in Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, which, in retrospect, was incredibly dangerous.

Amid the brouhaha, owner Jeffrey Lurie released a statement about his entry to the Eagles Hall of Fame.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"My induction into the Eagles Hall of Fame will always be a moment I look back on with immense pride. To join such a legendary group of individuals who have helped shape this franchise is an incredible honor and one that fills me with gratitude," wrote Lurie.

"To our coaches, players, and front office, and to everyone who has proudly represented this organization, I am deeply grateful for your dedication, commitment, and shared pursuit of excellence."

Fans quickly slammed Lurie, who bought the Eagles in 1994, for his tone-deaf letter.

"Kind of ironic to describe the Eagles this way and still not release a statement or speak to the press on Jalen. We deserve answers," said @AshdeeDietz.

"Jeff, gonna address the elephant in the room?" asked @adcparker.

"Congrats, but don't try to distract us from that medical team situation. WE WANT ANSWERS," demanded @ladub__.

"Jeff has been a good owner overall, but this is the worst time for this induction to happen," posted @TannerJPlummer.

"If you own the team, aren't you putting yourself in the hall?" stated @Yubyub69.

"Had time to make this statement, but not a statement about Jalen, LOL," commented @Icy7Trea.

Lurie and general manager Howie Roseman have stayed peculiarly mum on the issue surrounding Hurts, who led the Eagles to the title in 2025.

Moreover, Philadelphia has not made its medical team available to the media.

The NFL and the NFL Players Association have released a joint statement, stressing that they will review the matter.

articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers appeared to pull back the curtain on what NFL owners had proposed in the past regarding the International Series.

"There was talk about doing a week — an international week — where you had games in 16 different places and you just added an extra bye week," he said, per ESPN.com . "So you play 16 regular-season [weeks], you have two bye weeks — one of those weeks would've been an international week.

"I think it would've been phenomenal for the game. Now the owners wanted to push for 17 games for the extra revenue and because they care so much about player safety, but it would've been nice."
